# Trends track: what should shape the sagae-tools viewer (as of 2026-10-31)

Scope: changes in roughly the last 12-18 months, turned into adoptable ideas for the read-only KB viewer, plus what they imply for the gateway. Nothing third-party was installed or executed. Metadata came from the GitHub API, npm and PyPI. A few upstream files (source, README, LICENSE, the MCP matrix) were read through the GitHub API without being run. "Activity" below means the repo's `pushed_at`, which is a proxy for commit activity. Items marked **(my inference)** are design reasoning, not sourced facts.

## 1. Bottom line

1. **The biggest design risk is in the contract, not the renderer.** Wikidata and Graphiti both separate "true then, not now" from "recorded wrongly". The KB's single `status: superseded` merges the two. Fix this before any schema freeze (M4).
2. **Make time a global query context, not a separate view.** XTDB's "every query runs against some basis" is the right mental model. Every endpoint takes the two cursors, and every view state lives in the URL (M3, M12).
3. **The overview should be a map of communities, not a hairball.** Hierarchical Leiden is the proven default (GraphRAG). Compute it once in batch, and treat positions as stored data so time travel filters a stable picture (M1, M2).
4. **Claim-level trust is the product's differentiator, and it is cheap.** Statement cards, a quote hover, one click to a highlighted source, and a machine re-check of the quote. A study at AAAI 2025 found even random citations raise trust, and that trust falls only when people actually check. So the UI must make checking effortless (M5-M7).
5. **The feed and a health view come from the LLM-wiki pattern.** `log.md` maps to a cursor-based change feed and `lint` maps to saved health filters (M8, M11).
6. **Korean search must handle 2-syllable nouns.** FTS5 trigram alone returns nothing for them. Use bigrams, plus choseong typeahead on entity names, and test on a small golden set (M10).
7. **Skip the fashionable parts:** LLM chat in the viewer, GraphRAG or Graphiti as a backend, generative UI, continuous-zoom research, and a full RDF/PROV stack.
8. **The gateway got simpler.** MCP spec 2026-07-28 removed sessions and added `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` routing headers. This also weakens the case for a heavy MCP gateway product (section 7, my inference). MCP Apps is optional: the community matrix shows Claude web, Desktop, VS Code, ChatGPT, Cursor and Goose, but not Claude Code.

## 2. What changed, with dates

| When | Change | Why it matters here | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-01 | Zep paper formalises a bi-temporal graph with episode, entity and community tiers | Nearest published model to this KB | https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13956 |
| 2025-01 | "Citations and Trust in LLM Generated Responses" (AAAI 2025) | Citations raise trust even when random, and trust falls on checking | https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.01303 |
| 2025-05 to 07 | Embedding Atlas paper and open-source release | Density plus auto-label map became a free local component | https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06386 |
| 2025-06 | CSS Custom Highlight API reached Baseline | Quote highlighting without DOM mutation | https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CSS_Custom_Highlight_API |
| 2025-08 | Obsidian Bases public (1.9.10) | Table-over-properties became a norm in note tools | https://obsidian.md/changelog/2025-08-18-desktop-v1.9.10/ |
| 2026-01-26 | MCP Apps spec marked Stable | Tools can render iframe UI in hosts | https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps |
| 2026-02 | GraphRAG-Bench paper revised (v3): GraphRAG "often performs worse" than vanilla RAG in recent studies | Do not build the viewer around GraphRAG | https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05690 |
| 2026-04 | Karpathy's LLM Wiki gist (the page says created April 4; secondary sources say April 2-3) | Agent-maintained KBs went mainstream, and it asks for lint and log operations | https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f |
| 2026-06-17 | Google: A2UI + MCP Apps patterns (payload shows v0.9) | Generative UI is still moving | https://developers.googleblog.com/a2ui-and-mcp-apps/ |
| 2026-07-28 | MCP spec is stateless; sessions and `initialize` removed | Rewrites the gateway problem | https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog |
| 2026-09-08 | `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` 2.0 (GitHub release date) | Wire protocol unchanged from 1.x per README | https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps |
| 2026-10-08 | sigma 4.0.0: WebGL 2, SDF labels, heatmap layer, declarative styles | Materially changes the map approach, but is 3 weeks old | https://github.com/jacomyal/sigma.js/releases |
| 2026-10-05 | cosmos.gl 3.5.1 (v3 moved to luma.gl, WebGL 2) | Remains the option if scale grows | https://github.com/cosmosgl/graph |

## 3. Must-have ideas

### M1. Map-first overview with hierarchical communities
- **What:** At overview zoom, show community regions (density or hulls) with labels and aggregated inter-community links. Hide individual edges until the user zooms in or selects something. Two or three discrete levels are enough.
- **Source:** GraphRAG's `communities` table has `level`, `parent`, `children`, `size` (https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/index/outputs/). Its implementation calls `graspologic_native.hierarchical_leiden` with `max_cluster_size=10` and a fixed seed (https://github.com/microsoft/graphrag/blob/main/packages/graphrag/graphrag/graphs/hierarchical_leiden.py). sigma 4 has `@sigma/layer-webgl` heatmap layers, `labelVisibility` and SDF labels (https://github.com/jacomyal/sigma.js/releases).
- **Older basis:** Top-down hierarchy navigation with animation to preserve the mental map (https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/4297211/).
- **View:** Graph overview, neighbor expansion.
- **Cost:** Medium.
- **Contract:** Yes. An overview artifact per basis: node `x,y`, community path per level, community `title`, `size`, `top_members`, `layout_version`.
- **Licence trap:** `vtraag/leidenalg` is GPL-3.0. `graspologic-native` is MIT (1.3.1, 2026-06-14). If a JS-only path is needed, `graphology-communities-louvain` 2.0.2 is MIT but last changed 2024-12. There is no npm `graphology-communities-leiden` (404).
- **Note:** I found no 2025-26 peer-reviewed paper that combines Leiden, semantic zoom and KG sensemaking. This idea rests on practice and older visualisation work.

### M2. Positions are stored data
- **What:** Do not run layout at render time on the overview. Persist positions, version them, and place new nodes near their neighbours. Point-in-time then changes visibility and colour, not geometry. **(my inference; the mental-map rationale comes from the M1 reference.)**
- **Source:** sigma takes positions from graph attributes, and cosmos.gl has `setPointPositions()` (https://github.com/cosmosgl/graph). Graphiti's experience is a warning for the batch side: incremental community assignment drifts, so "periodic community refreshes remain necessary" (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13956v1).
- **View:** Overview, point-in-time, change feed.
- **Cost:** Low.
- **Contract:** Yes, a small one: `layout_version`, and stable community IDs across refreshes (fixed seed, plus overlap matching to previous IDs).

### M3. One global time basis across all views
- **What:** Two cursors, `valid_at` and `observed_at`, default to now/latest, shown persistently in the header and encoded in the URL. Each view honours them. An "Any" mode shows all versions. A banner appears whenever the viewer is not at latest.
- **Source:** XTDB's `SETTING DEFAULT VALID_TIME ..., DEFAULT SYSTEM_TIME ...` and "every query runs against some basis" (https://docs.xtdb.com/quickstart/sql-overview.html). Datomic's `asOf`, `since` and `history` (https://docs.datomic.com/reference/filters.html). The Now/date/Any selector comes from minigraf-visualizer (https://github.com/project-minigraf/minigraf-visualizer).
- **View:** All, especially point-in-time.
- **Cost:** Medium. Viewer plumbing is low, and the KB queries are the real cost.
- **Contract:** Yes. Every read endpoint accepts both cursors and echoes the resolved `basis`. Pagination is pinned to that basis.
- **Open semantic issue:** Graphiti's T′ is when the system ingested a fact. The KB's "observed time" may instead mean when a source was seen, like Wikidata's `retrieved` (P813). For back-filled data these differ. If both matter, there are three timestamps, not two.

### M4. Separate "changed in the world" from "was wrong"
- **What:** A closed validity interval means the fact was right then. A correction means it was never right. These must look different and must behave differently in point-in-time: a corrected value should still appear when viewing old `observed_at`, but not in current belief about that past.
- **Source:** Wikidata: "Correct historical values should not be deprecated", use start and end time qualifiers; deprecated means erroneous or outdated, and reasons go in P2241 (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Help:Ranking). Graphiti keeps `t_invalid` (world) apart from `t'expired` (system) (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13956v1). GraphRAG claims carry `status` TRUE, FALSE or SUSPECTED (https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/index/outputs/).
- **View:** Entity detail, history, point-in-time.
- **Cost:** Low in the viewer.
- **Contract:** Yes, and this is the highest-priority ask. Replace or refine `superseded` with a reason enum such as `world_changed`, `corrected`, `source_retracted`. Define `dead` precisely. Consider a Wikidata-like rank for concurrent values.

### M5. Statement cards as the page atom
- **What:** Entity pages are predicate groups rather than prose: best value first, "n other values" collapsed, then validity range, rank icon, references, origin chip.
- **Source:** Wikidata's statement, qualifier, reference and rank model. "Best rank" is preferred if one exists, otherwise normal, and deprecated is excluded by default (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Help:Ranking, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Help:Sources).
- **View:** Entity detail, table view.
- **Cost:** Low to medium.
- **Contract:** Yes. A claim needs a stable `predicate`, typed `value` and, if available, `qualifiers`. The KB should return a server-computed `best` flag so every client agrees.

### M6. Citation pill, quote on hover, highlighted source on click
- **What:** Each claim has a small numbered source pill. Hover shows the verbatim quote. Click opens the snapshot scrolled to the highlighted quote.
- **Source:** NotebookLM (now also labelled Gemini Notebook): hover shows quoted text, selection opens the source viewer and auto-scrolls to it (https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16179559?hl=en). Trust finding: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.01303. Highlight mechanism: `CSS.highlights`, no DOM mutation, but no semantics for assistive tech (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CSS_Custom_Highlight_API).
- **View:** Entity detail, source view.
- **Cost:** Low.
- **Contract:** Yes. Snapshot text is retrievable by ID; see M7.

### M7. Robust quote anchors and a visible check
- **What:** Store a W3C-style anchor (`exact`, `prefix`, `suffix`, optional `start`, `end`) and snapshot hash. The viewer re-checks each quote against the snapshot and shows verified, relocated or missing. Offsets alone are brittle, and a verbatim quote from an LLM is a claim until checked.
- **Source:** W3C `TextQuoteSelector`, `TextPositionSelector`, and `TimeState` with `sourceDate`, `cached` (https://www.w3.org/TR/annotation-model/). The Claude Citations API returns `cited_text` with `start_char_index` and guarantees valid pointers into the provided documents, which is a cheap way for KB ingest to get these (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations).
- **View:** Source view, health view.
- **Cost:** Low.
- **Contract:** Yes. `quote.selector`, `snapshot_id`, `snapshot_sha256`, and a defined text normalisation (NFC). HTML snapshots need a rule for what text the offsets apply to.

### M8. Change feed as an ordered log with a cursor
- **What:** Monotonic sequence, grouped by ingest run, with per-run +/- counts. Filter by origin and actor. The client polls with a cursor every 30-60s, and an unchanged result costs almost nothing.
- **Source:** Datomic: the log is a time index, and an instant is "not as precise as" t or tx values (https://docs.datomic.com/reference/filters.html). LLM Wiki's append-only `log.md` (gist). Minigraf's transaction log with `+`/`−` counts. Graphiti's episode links (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13956v1).
- **View:** Change feed.
- **Cost:** Low.
- **Contract:** Yes. `GET /changes?since=<seq>&limit=` returns `seq`, `run_id`, `actor`, op, target and a before/after pointer. Never use a timestamp as the cursor. Also add an ETag or equivalent.

### M9. Minimal provenance actor
- **What:** Every claim shows who or what produced it and in which run: person, or model plus version, with a link to the run. This is the PROV shape without RDF.
- **Source:** PROV-DM's Entity, Activity and Agent with `wasGeneratedBy`, `used`, `wasAttributedTo`; Revision and Quotation are subtypes of derivation (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/). Nanopublications split assertion, provenance and publication info (https://nanopub.net/guidelines/working_draft/). The LLM Wiki gist has thin provenance, and critics argue LLM-only upkeep compounds errors (secondary source: https://www.implicator.ai/karpathys-llm-wiki-got-16-million-views-the-code-isnt-the-point-2.md).
- **View:** Entity detail, change feed.
- **Cost:** Low.
- **Contract:** Yes. `generated_by: {agent_type, agent_id, model?, run_id}`, kept separate from `origin`.

### M10. Korean search in layers
- **What, in order:**
  1. **Normalise:** Convert queries and stored text to NFC. "검색" is 2 code points in NFC and 6 in NFD, and the two forms are not equal in JS (tested locally in node 26). NFD arrives from macOS and from some web text.
  2. **Entity typeahead, client-side:** Aliases plus choseong matching (ㄱㅅ matches 검색) over about 10k names, using `es-hangul`.
  3. **Body search with bigrams:** Pre-tokenise into a dedicated FTS column in application code, so no native SQLite extension is needed. This covers 2-syllable nouns and compounds such as 정보검색. **(my inference; untested on real data.)**
  4. **Optional precision layer:** Add Kiwi morpheme tokens in a second, higher-weighted column.
  5. **Results at claim level:** Include snippet offsets, respect the time basis, and default to active claims with a toggle for superseded.
- **Source:**
  - FTS5: substrings under 3 characters match no rows; custom tokenizers need C (https://sqlite.org/fts5.html).
  - A small Korean benchmark (40 docs, 28 queries, self-reported) found trigram recall@5 of 0.2857 against 1.0, the whole gap coming from queries under 3 characters. On longer queries the two were equal (https://docs.rs/crate/llm-kernel/latest/source/docs/benchmarks/korean-recall.md).
  - Lucene CJK bigrams explicitly cover Hangul (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/text-analysis/analysis-cjk-bigram-tokenfilter).
  - Kiwi has a WASM build on npm (`kiwi-nlp` 0.24.1, 2026-10-19, 5.6MB unpacked; model file size not checked) (https://github.com/bab2min/Kiwi).
- **Local test:** `Intl.Segmenter` leaves particles attached: "검색엔진을 | 지식그래프의 | 이력을". So browser segmentation alone will not do.
- **View:** Search, table search box.
- **Cost:** Medium.
- **Contract:** Yes. A `/search` endpoint that hides the engine, an `aliases[]` field (needed for 깃허브/GitHub), and match offsets in the response.
- **Test first:** Build about 30 golden Korean queries on the real corpus before picking analyzers. The KB ADR on storage decides where this runs.

### M11. Health view as saved filters
- **What:** Presets over the table view: orphans, unsourced claims, unverified quotes (M7), overlapping contradictory values, stale claims, sources that went dead.
- **Source:** The LLM Wiki `lint` op checks for "contradictions between pages" and "stale claims that newer sources have superseded", and it uses the graph view to spot hubs and orphans (gist). Graphiti detects temporally overlapping contradictions (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13956v1).
- **View:** Table view (preset tab). This is not a new view.
- **Cost:** Low.
- **Contract:** Partial. Contradiction detection needs predicate cardinality (single or multi-valued). Otherwise the KB emits lint results.

### M12. Deep links as the agent-to-viewer interface
- **What:** Every state (entity, time basis, filter, highlighted quote) is a shareable URL. MCP tools return these URLs alongside text. This is the cheap version of agent-native UI, and it works in a terminal.
- **Source:** The MCP extension matrix has no check for Claude Code under MCP Apps (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/docs/extensions/client-matrix.mdx). The matrix is community-maintained.
- **View:** All.
- **Cost:** Low.
- **Contract:** No. IDs must be stable.

## 4. Nice-to-have ideas

| ID | Idea and source | View | Cost | Contract need |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | **Bitemporal map:** each claim version is a box, valid time across, recorded time up; dragging moves both cursors. Scope it to one entity or predicate. https://github.com/project-minigraf/minigraf-visualizer | History | Low-medium | None beyond M3 |
| N2 | **Scrubber with snapping and diff colours:** snaps to dates where facts start or stop; green and red for added and removed. Same source. | Point-in-time, overview | Medium | `/timeline` date histogram |
| N3 | **Compare two bases:** the claims that differ between A and B. Datomic `since` pattern. https://docs.datomic.com/reference/filters.html | Point-in-time, change feed | Low-medium | `/changes?from&to` |
| N4 | **Community summaries with citations:** GraphRAG `community_reports` (`title`, `summary`, `rank`, `findings`). Tag them as derived. https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/index/outputs/ | Overview | Medium | `summary`, `source_claim_ids` |
| N5 | **Multi-level names via Toponymy** (beta, needs vectors, 2D map, LLM). https://github.com/TutteInstitute/toponymy | Overview labels | Medium | Same as N4, computed in batch |
| N6 | **Embedding map tab:** Embedding Atlas `EmbeddingView` takes `x,y`, optional `category`, and manual `labels` with `level` and `priority`. It reveals near-duplicates that the graph does not link. No edges documented. https://apple.github.io/embedding-atlas/embedding-view.html | Second overview tab | Medium | `x,y` or embeddings |
| N7 | **Crossfilter facets with Mosaic and DuckDB-WASM** over a static Parquet export. This also suits a no-daemon KB. https://github.com/uwdata/mosaic | Table view | Medium | Parquet or Arrow export |
| N8 | **MCP Apps card:** `ui://kb/entity` reuses the viewer component. `_meta.ui.resourceUri`, CSP restrictive by default, `visibility: ["app"]` for app-only tools. https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps | Entity card in chat | Medium | None |
| N9 | **Hybrid semantic search:** KURE-v1 modestly beats bge-m3 on its own card, and newer models lead a Korean leaderboard. Re-check before choosing. https://huggingface.co/nlpai-lab/KURE-v1, https://discuss.pytorch.kr/t/ko-embedding-leaderboard/11416 | Search | Medium-high | Embeddings, hybrid endpoint |
| N10 | **Saved views as plain files** in the repo, as Obsidian Bases does with notes as a database. https://obsidian.md/changelog/2025-08-18-desktop-v1.9.10/ | Table view | Low | None |

**Korean warning for N5 and N6:** Embedding Atlas's `TextSummarizer` uses c-TF-IDF with `Intl.Segmenter` and an English stemmer (https://github.com/apple/embedding-atlas/blob/main/packages/component/src/lib/text_summarizer/text_summarizer.ts). Given the local segmenter test above, auto-labels on Korean would be particle-attached eojeol such as "지식그래프의". Pass your own labels through the `labels` prop with `autoLabelEnabled: false`.

## 5. Fashionable ideas to skip

| Skip | Why |
|---|---|
| **LLM chat or GraphRAG query box in the viewer** | The viewer is read-only and deterministic, and agents already reach the KB through MCP. Evidence for graph retrieval is mixed: recent studies report GraphRAG "often performs worse" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05690); a systematic evaluation finds "distinct strengths" by task (https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11371). |
| **Graphiti, GraphRAG or LightRAG as the backend** | The KB has its own claim model. Graphiti needs a graph DB and an LLM key, and its MCP server states it has no auth or prompt-injection protection (https://github.com/getzep/graphiti). LightRAG calls its file-based defaults test-only (https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG). Borrow schemas and UI, not the runtime. |
| **FastGraphRAG-style noun-phrase graphs** | Microsoft calls the result noisier, and the default NLP is mainly suited to English (https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/index/methods/). Wrong for Korean-capable claims with verbatim quotes. |
| **LazyGraphRAG** | I found no open-source release. Microsoft ships it through Discovery and Azure Local (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/project/graphrag/). |
| **Continuous zoom via heat diffusion and Poincaré embeddings** | A single-author preprint (https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2603.08965). Discrete levels suit about 10k nodes. |
| **GPU force simulation at this scale** | cosmos.gl targets hundreds of thousands of points, has no built-in labels, and is WebGL only. Labels matter more here, and M2 removes the need for live simulation. Revisit only if measurements fail. |
| **Nomic Atlas** | A hosted product. Python client last released 2025-11-11 (3.9.0), with no licence detected on the repo. Embedding Atlas covers local use. |
| **A2UI, AG-UI, generative UI** | Views are fixed, so runtime-generated UI adds risk without value. Versions are moving: the June blog shows v0.9, and the repo's latest tag is `cli-v0.1.0` from 2026-10-30. Hosts need a native renderer for two of the three patterns (https://developers.googleblog.com/a2ui-and-mcp-apps/). |
| **Full RDF, PROV-O or nanopublication stack** | Adopt the shape in M9. Formal graphs and signing serve inter-organisation exchange, which a solo KB does not need **(my inference)**. |
| **Elasticsearch with Nori** | A standard Korean analyzer path (mecab-ko-dic; https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/plugins/analysis-nori), but it adds an always-on cluster, against the KB's principle. |
| **XTDB or Datomic as storage for the viewer** | Take the query semantics only. Storage belongs to the KB's ADR. I did not evaluate their runtime needs. |
| **3D graph views, push-based live updates** | 3D is my judgement call, with no study behind it here. For updates, 30-60s polling already meets the stated target. |

## 6. Consolidated contract asks for the KB

Ranked by how much later pain each avoids.

| # | Ask | From |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Split `superseded` by reason, and define `dead` | M4 |
| C2 | Define the time fields exactly: valid from/to, observed, recorded. Decide whether observed and recorded differ | M3 |
| C3 | All reads take `valid_at`, `observed_at`; responses echo `basis` | M3 |
| C4 | `quote.selector` (`exact`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `start`, `end`), `snapshot_id`, hash, NFC rule | M7 |
| C5 | `/changes?since=<seq>` with `run_id`, `actor`; monotonic integer cursor | M8 |
| C6 | `generated_by` on claims, separate from `origin` | M9 |
| C7 | `predicate`, typed value, cardinality, server `best` flag, optional rank | M5, M11 |
| C8 | `aliases[]` on entities; `/search` hides the engine and returns offsets | M10 |
| C9 | Overview artifact with positions, community path, `layout_version` | M1, M2 |
| C10 | Fixtures must cover: a corrected value, a world-changed value, overlapping values, a back-filled claim with old valid time and new recorded time, a dead source, a Korean NFD quote, a 2-syllable query | All |

## 7. Gateway implications

- **Stateless MCP simplifies aggregation.** Sessions and the handshake are gone, and every request carries version and capabilities in `_meta` (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog). A thin gateway needs no sticky routing or session store.
- **Routing and logging without parsing bodies.** `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers are required on Streamable HTTP POST, and the MCP blog names gateways as a use (https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/). OTel `traceparent` conventions in `_meta` give request tracing.
- **Caching is built in.** `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` on list and read results fit a shared process well. `tools/list` should be deterministically ordered, which matters when merging servers.
- **Must pass through untouched (my inference):** `_meta.ui.*`, `ui://` reads, and the `extensions` capability field. If the aggregator prefixes tool names, it must still map resource URIs correctly, or MCP Apps break.
- **Mixed versions (my inference):** Servers on 2025-11-25 still use `initialize`. If any such server is kept, the gateway must speak both. Prefer writing in-repo servers against 2026-07-28 only.
- **Avoid deprecated parts.** Do not add Dynamic Client Registration (deprecated in favour of CIMD), Sampling, Roots or Logging.
- **Label untrusted content (my inference).** KB content with `origin: external` is untrusted text that reaches LLMs through MCP tools. Keep `origin` in tool results so agents can treat it as data. Graphiti's README warning (above) shows that this is not solved by default.
- **Viewer path.** The feed, cursor reads and static overview artifacts in section 6 are cacheable, so the gateway can stay a small, single always-on process in front of file-based KB reads.

## 8. Shortlist status

| Project | Release | Licence | Activity | Runtime | No Docker? | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sigma | 4.0.4, 2026-10-27 (4.0.0 on 2026-10-08) | MIT | 2026-10-27 | Browser, WebGL 2 | Yes | Adopt as candidate. Very new major, with breaking changes |
| graspologic-native | 1.3.1, 2026-06-14 | MIT | 2026-06-14 | Python wheel; exact Python range not determined | Yes, expected | Adopt for batch Leiden |
| es-hangul | 2.4.0, npm change 2026-08-24 | MIT | 2026-08-27 | Node or browser | Yes | Adopt |
| kiwi-nlp / Kiwi | 0.24.1, 2026-10-19 | Apache-2.0 | 2026-10-27 | WASM from npm | Yes | Adapt, optional precision layer |
| Embedding Atlas | 0.26.0, 2026-10-15 | MIT | 2026-10-29 | npm components or Python tool; WebGPU renderer present in repo | Yes | Adapt, later tab |
| @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps | 2.0.4, 2026-10-27 | Moving MIT to Apache-2.0; npm says MIT | 2026-10-29 | Node 20+ | Yes | Adapt, optional |
| Mosaic | 0.34.3, 2026-10-29 | GitHub shows NOASSERTION; not checked further | 2026-10-30 | Browser with DuckDB-WASM | Yes, expected | Adapt, optional |
| Toponymy | 0.5.4, 2026-09-04 | MIT | 2026-10-26 | Python >=3.10, embedder, LLM; beta | Yes | Adapt, optional |
| minigraf-visualizer | No release read; last commit 2026-09-27 | Apache-2.0 or MIT | 14 commits, 0 stars | React, WASM | Yes | Design reference only |
| cosmos.gl | 3.5.1, 2026-10-05 | MIT | 2026-10-29 | Browser, WebGL 2, luma.gl ~9.3 | Yes | Reject for now, fallback |
| Graphiti | 0.31.2, 2026-10-20 | Apache-2.0 | 2026-10-28 | Python >=3.10, graph DB, LLM key | Yes; Docker optional, FalkorDB Lite embedded | Reject as dependency, adopt the model |
| GraphRAG | 3.3.0, 2026-10-08 | MIT | 2026-10-29 | Python, LLM; versions not verified | Not determined, likely | Reject as dependency, adopt the schema |
| LightRAG | 1.5.7, 2026-09-02 | MIT | 2026-10-29 | Python, LLM | Yes | Reject |
| XTDB | 2.2.0, 2026-10-21 | MPL-2.0 | 2026-10-30 | Not determined | Not determined | Reject here, borrow the query idea |
| A2UI | cli-v0.1.0, 2026-10-30 | Apache-2.0 | 2026-10-31 | Host renderer | Not relevant | Reject |

## 9. Limits of this research

- **Embedding Atlas paper:** The PDF text would not decode, so I only confirmed the abstract page. Details come from docs and the repo tree. "WebGPU with WebGL 2 fallback" is from a secondary source; the repo does contain a `webgpu_renderer` directory.
- **Sigma and cosmos.gl:** No performance figures are stated for sigma 4. Neither has been measured at 10k nodes and 50k edges with labels in this project.
- **Graph RAG papers:** I read abstracts only. arXiv 2503.04338 lists no venue on its page, so I did not cite it as a VLDB paper.
- **Korean:** The benchmark is tiny and self-reported. I found no primary comparison of mecab-ko and trigram, and no Kiwi-based FTS5 tokenizer. The bigram design in M10 is untested.
- **MCP Apps support:** The matrix is community-maintained. Treat the Claude Code gap as "not listed", and re-check.
- **LLM Wiki scale limits:** Reported limits of 200 or 1,000 files come from secondary sources and conflict, so I did not use them.
- **Secondary sources:** These were used only to find primary sources, except where marked.

# HTTP gateway track: one entry point, access, lifecycle, KB hosting

Date: 2026-10-31. Scope: the non-MCP half of the gateway and how it stays running.
Local measurements were made on this machine (WSL2, 24 vCPU, Ubuntu 26.04, bun 1.4.4, node 26.13.0) with already-installed runtimes only. No third-party code was installed. Scripts are in `scratchpad/research/bench/`.

## 1. Verdict

1. **One process is enough to start.** Run one Hono app that serves the viewer UI, the viewer backend, the KB read API and `/mcp`. Do not put Caddy, Traefik or Envoy in front.
2. **Why no proxy.** No proxy can host the KB read code. Something must run application code anyway, and that same thing can route. A proxy adds a process and config language without removing either.
3. **One exception.** If the MCP track picks agentgateway for aggregation, use two processes: agentgateway in front (it does route plain HTTP) and the Hono app as its backend. Caddy is still not needed.
4. **KB needs no daemon.** The gateway can host the HTTP read surface. In-process library, per-request CLI spawn and socket-activated service all beat p95 < 200 ms on a synthetic graph (section 5). Latency does not decide this. Coupling does.
5. **Runtime: Node 26, not Bun, if socket activation is wanted.** `Bun.serve({fd:3})` on 1.4.4 silently ignores the fd and binds port 3000 (measured). Node `listen({fd:3})` works, with about 45 ms cold first response.
6. **Socket activation does not wake WSL.** It gives "no process until first hit" only inside a running distro. Nothing here makes a Windows browser boot WSL.
7. **Access: localhost now, Tailscale Serve when another device needs it.** Static bearer token for MCP. No oauth2-proxy or Pomerium.

## 2. Minimal architecture

```
Windows browser ──────────┐
Claude Code (WSL) ────────┤
Other tailnet device ─ tailscale serve (later, optional) ─┤
                          v
             127.0.0.1:8787  (systemd user .socket)
                          v  on first connection
             sagae-gateway: Hono on Node 26, exits after idle
               /             static viewer build (serveStatic)
               /api/viewer   viewer backend (route module, same process)
               /api/kb/v1    KB read surface, implements the KB OpenAPI contract
                             via KbReader: library | CLI | child process
               /mcp/*        MCP servers mounted in-process, or forwarded
               /healthz
             middleware: Host/Origin allow-list, bearer auth on /mcp, request log
```

All of it is library use, not a hand-written proxy. Hono 4.13.14 exports `bearer-auth`, `cors`, `logger`, `proxy`, `secure-headers`, `serve-static`, `ip-restriction`, `timeout` and `streaming` (checked with `npm view hono exports`). `@hono/node-server` exports `createAdaptorServer` ([source](https://github.com/honojs/node-server/blob/main/src/index.ts)) and `serveStatic`.

Viewer backend and KB read API as route modules means one crash domain. That is acceptable for read-only personal use. A separate process can come later without changing URLs.

Caddy facts, for later use:
- [Flushes `text/event-stream` immediately](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy) and supports unix-socket upstreams.
- Has socket activation through `bind fd/3`. The [conventions page](https://caddyserver.com/docs/conventions) does not list them.

agentgateway can mix an MCP route and a plain host route on one listener ([routes doc](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/documentation/configuration/routes.md)). Its [MCP auth](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/documentation/mcp/mcp-authn.md) validates tokens from an external authorization server.

### One process or proxy plus MCP gateway

| Layout | Processes | Operating cost | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hono only | 1 | One codebase, one unit pair | Default. MCP servers are few and mounted in-process, or at separate `/mcp/<name>` paths |
| agentgateway → Hono | 2 | One YAML, plus Hono. Front is always on, Hono can stay socket-activated at `host: 127.0.0.1:8788` | MCP track wants tool aggregation or stdio supervision |
| Caddy → Hono | 2 | Caddyfile plus one more binary to update | Only for LAN-wide TLS or several unrelated apps. Tailscale Serve covers TLS |
| Caddy → agentgateway → Hono | 3 | Three configs for one user | Never |

Keep separate `/mcp/<name>` paths until a single merged endpoint is shown to be needed. Claude Code handles several entries natively (`claude mcp add` per path).

### MCP protocol effect on the gateway

- Current revision is [2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning). [Streamable HTTP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/transports/streamable-http) dropped the GET stream and protocol sessions. Each message is one POST.
- This suits idle exit: a restart loses no session state. Older revisions up to 2025-11-25 had `Mcp-Session-Id`, so mount any legacy-era server in stateless mode, or expect session loss on idle exit.
- `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers let an intermediary route or log without parsing bodies.
- `subscriptions/listen` is a long-lived SSE stream. Count open streams as activity in the idle timer. I did not determine whether Claude Code opens one.
- The spec requires `Origin` validation (403 if present and invalid), says local servers should bind to 127.0.0.1, and says servers should authenticate.
- Servers should send `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and periodic `:` SSE comments on long streams.

**Bun pitfall if Bun is used anywhere:** [Bun.serve closes idle connections after 10 s by default](https://bun.com/docs/guides/http/sse), and a quiet SSE stream counts as idle. Use `server.timeout(req, 0)` or set `idleTimeout`. [Field reports](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/27479) put the maximum at 255 s, with 0 disabling it.

## 3. Access and auth

### Reachability

| Mode | Setup | Reachable from | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Localhost** | None. This host already has `networkingMode=Mirrored` in `.wslconfig` | Windows browser, WSL tools | **Adopt now** |
| **Tailscale Serve** | Install Tailscale, then `tailscale serve --bg 8787` | Own tailnet devices only | **Next step** when phone or laptop access is wanted |
| **Cloudflare Tunnel + Access** | Domain on Cloudflare, `cloudflared` | Public internet behind Access | Only if a Claude cloud connector is wanted |

Localhost notes:
- In [mirrored mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/networking) Windows and WSL reach each other over `127.0.0.1`. In NAT mode `localhost` forwarding also works, with [`localhostForwarding` default true](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config).
- Bind `127.0.0.1` explicitly. Microsoft notes `::1` is not supported for Linux reaching Windows; do not assume it the other way either.
- Mirrored mode lets [Windows ports block Linux binds](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config) (see `ignoredPorts`). Pick a quiet port.
- Mirrored mode also allows LAN access once Hyper-V firewall rules are opened. A `127.0.0.1` bind avoids that.

Tailscale Serve notes:
- [Provisions TLS for the tailnet name and adds `Tailscale-User-Login`](https://tailscale.com/kb/1312/serve). It strips client-supplied copies, so a backend bound to localhost can trust the header.
- [`--bg` persists across reboots; `--set-path` maps paths](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/tailscale-cli/serve).
- Serve is config on `tailscaled`, not a process of ours, but `tailscaled` is itself always on.
- Tailscale is not installed in WSL, and not at the default Windows path. I could not confirm from primary sources whether Serve on the Windows host reaches a WSL `127.0.0.1` service in mirrored mode, or whether `tailscaled` inside WSL is the better placement. Test before relying on it.

Cloud connector note:
- [Claude custom connectors connect from Anthropic's cloud](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp), so a tailnet or localhost server fails. [Hostnames resolving to private or CGNAT addresses are rejected](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/troubleshooting).
- Claude Code in WSL has no such limit because it connects locally.
- For public exposure: Cloudflare Access [Managed OAuth](https://blog.cloudflare.com/managed-oauth-for-access) or Anthropic's [MCP tunnels](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/mcp-tunnels/overview) (documented as subject to change).
- [Secure MCP servers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/ai-controls/secure-mcp-servers/) requires a hostname proxied through Cloudflare DNS, and Managed OAuth only for servers that validate the Access JWT.
- Not determined: free-plan seat limits and whether these features are on the free plan.

### What Claude Code requires

From the [Claude Code MCP docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp):
- `--transport http` is the recommended remote transport. SSE is deprecated. WebSocket goes through `add-json`.
- Static auth: `claude mcp add --transport http sagae http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`. With a configured `Authorization` header, Claude Code does not fall back to OAuth.
- `.mcp.json` headers support `${VAR}` expansion. `headersHelper` runs a command per connection and re-runs on 401 or 403.
- OAuth needs RFC 9728 metadata, then RFC 8414. Dynamic registration is the default; pre-configured `--client-id`, `--callback-port` and CIMD are also supported.
- Reconnect: up to 5 attempts mid-session, up to 3 retries on first connection. Connection refused during a WSL restart recovers within that window only if the gateway returns quickly.
- Tool calls abort after 5 minutes of silence on HTTP. Output limit defaults to 25,000 tokens.

[MCP authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/authorization) is optional. So a static bearer token is valid for a personal setup. A public OAuth setup must implement Protected Resource Metadata and audience-bound tokens.

### Auth choice

| Layer | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| All routes | Host and Origin allow-list | Blocks DNS rebinding from any site in the Windows browser. Required for MCP, cheap for the rest |
| `/mcp/*` | Static bearer token via `hono/bearer-auth`, stored in an `EnvironmentFile` mode 600 | Works with Claude Code today with no IdP |
| Viewer UI and APIs, localhost | No login | Read-only, loopback-bound, same-user machine |
| Viewer UI and APIs, Tailscale | Check `Tailscale-User-Login` | Identity for free, no login page |
| **oauth2-proxy** v7.15.5, 2026-10-01, MIT | **Reject for now** | Needs an OIDC provider. Its [`skip_jwt_bearer_tokens`](https://oauth2-proxy.github.io/oauth2-proxy/configuration/overview/) only passes verified JWTs, not static tokens |
| **Pomerium** v0.33.6, 2026-10-27, Apache-2.0 | **Reject for now** | [Linux tarball, no Docker needed, but the sample config expects an IdP](https://www.pomerium.com/docs/deploy/core). Real [MCP gateway features](https://www.pomerium.com/docs/capabilities/mcp) serve multi-user, upstream OAuth cases. Revisit if the setup goes public |

## 4. Lifecycle on WSL2

### Facts that shape the design

- ["systemd services will NOT keep your WSL instance alive."](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/systemd)
- [`[general] instanceIdleTimeout`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config) defaults to 15000 ms; -1 disables it. `[wsl2] vmIdleTimeout` defaults to 60000 ms and is Windows 11 only.
- `wsl --shutdown` stops all distros at once ([wsl-config](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config)).
- [WSL issue 13291](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/13291): `vmIdleTimeout=-1` alone was not enough. The thread's fix sets both keys, and a maintainer edited his message to match.
- Field reports say [a `wsl.exe` client must exist or the distro stops within seconds](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/discussions/9245). Common fix: a logon task running `wsl.exe -d <distro> --exec sleep infinity`, unticking the 3-day task limit.

Observed on this host: systemd on, `Linger=no`, no idle keys in `.wslconfig`, `autoMemoryReclaim=Gradual`, memory cap 48 GB. The installed WSL version was not checked; latest release is 3.0.3 (2026-10-09).

### What happens when

| Event | Result |
|---|---|
| Last WSL client exits | Distro stops after about 15 s by default. Gateway and socket unit die. |
| Viewer tab keeps polling | Inference, not documented: polling does not count as a client, so the tab starts failing. Show an "offline" state. |
| `wsl --shutdown` or Windows reboot | Everything stops. Nothing restarts until something launches WSL. |
| WSL restarts | Enabled socket units come back if the user manager runs, which needs `loginctl enable-linger sagae`. |
| Connection to a stopped WSL | Inference: a socket unit is a listener inside the VM, so nothing is listening and the connection fails. I found no primary statement that a localhost connection boots WSL. Assume it does not. Not tested, because testing from inside WSL requires stopping it. |
| Windows sleep or hibernate | Not researched. |

### Service manager

| Option | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **systemd user units + linger** | **Adopt** | Already running here. Socket activation, restart, journald, no new dependency. Same model in a Proxmox LXC |
| **systemd socket activation** | **Adopt**, via Node | Fits the KB's minimal-always-on principle |
| **pm2** 7.1.1, 2026-10-23 | **Reject** | Its own daemon, and [`pm2 startup` is itself systemd](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/startup/) on this host, so it adds a layer. No socket activation benefit. npm metadata lists AGPL-3.0 |

Sketch:

```ini
# ~/.config/systemd/user/sagae-gateway.socket
[Socket]
ListenStream=127.0.0.1:8787
[Install]
WantedBy=sockets.target

# ~/.config/systemd/user/sagae-gateway.service
[Service]
ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/node %h/sagae-tools/apps/gateway/dist/main.js
EnvironmentFile=%h/.config/sagae-gateway/env
Restart=on-failure
```

```ts
const server = createAdaptorServer({ fetch: app.fetch });
if (process.env.LISTEN_FDS === "1") server.listen({ fd: 3 });
else server.listen(8787, "127.0.0.1");
```

- Idle exit is app code: exit 0 when no request or open stream for N minutes. Set N above the 30-60 s poll, for example 10 minutes. The socket stays armed by systemd.
- With `Accept=no`, [one service handles all connections](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.socket.html).
- Node is under nvm here, so use a stable symlink rather than a versioned path.
- The Hono adapter path was not tested, because nothing third-party could be installed. A bare `node:http` server with `listen({fd:3})` was.

### Bun and socket activation

- Measured on bun 1.4.4: `Bun.serve({fd:3})` logged `3000 localhost` and clients timed out, 10 of 10. It ignored the fd without an error.
- Matches open issues: [#22559](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/22559) and PR [#44013](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/44013).
- Workaround tested: a shell shim starts Bun on a private port and execs [`systemd-socket-proxyd`](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-socket-proxyd.html). 7 of 10 runs took 16-19 ms; 3 took about 1.02 s, cause not diagnosed. It works but adds a moving part.
- Tradeoff: Bun starts faster and uses less memory (below), but Node gives working activation with no shim. Hono keeps the switch to a few lines, so this is reversible once #44013 lands.

### Keep-alive policy

1. **Level 0, default.** No keep-alive. The gateway works whenever a WSL session is open, which matches daily use with Claude Code.
2. **Level 1, if the viewer must work with no terminal.** Set `[general] instanceIdleTimeout=-1` and `[wsl2] vmIdleTimeout=-1`, plus a logon task that boots the distro. Cost: these are global, and the VM stays resident. Weigh this against the KB principle, because it trades one small process for a whole always-on VM.
3. **Level 2, if it must work with the PC off.** Move to a Proxmox LXC.

### Moving to Proxmox LXC later

- Same units, converted to system units with `User=`. Socket activation behaves the same, and a real always-on host removes the WSL problems above.
- Tailscale in LXC: [pass through `/dev/net/tun`](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/containers/lxc/lxc-unprivileged), for example `pct set CTID --dev0 /dev/net/tun`.
- **KB data must move with the gateway when using a local DB.** [SQLite WAL requires all processes on one host and does not work over a network filesystem](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html). If the DB stays in WSL, the KB would then need a network read path.
- Keep the DB on ext4 inside WSL, never under `/mnt/c`.

## 5. KB integration: can the gateway host the read surface?

**Yes.** Measured on a synthetic SQLite graph: 10k nodes, 50k edges, 4.4 MB. A neighbor request returned 200 edges plus nodes, about 69 KB JSON. Client and server were in the same VM with a warm page cache.

| Path | p50 | p95 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-process, `bun:sqlite`, sequential | 1.0 ms | 1.7 ms | n=1000 |
| In-process, 8 concurrent | 3.4 ms | 5.7 ms | n=800 |
| In-process via one extra HTTP hop | 1.5 ms | 2.1 ms | A proxy costs about 0.4 ms |
| Overview dump, all nodes and edges, in-process | 13.6 ms | 20.3 ms | 2.1 MB JSON, n=30. Sync, blocks the event loop |
| Spawn CLI per request, Bun | 9.6 ms | 11.1 ms | n=100 |
| Spawn CLI, Bun, 8 concurrent | 26.0 ms | 40.8 ms | n=200 |
| Spawn CLI per request, Node | 24.9 ms | 28.8 ms | n=100 |
| Spawn CLI per request, Python stdlib | 24.4 ms | 40.8 ms | n=100, no third-party imports |
| Socket-activated Node, first request | about 45 ms (41.7-47.7) | n/a | One cold start, then in-process speed |

Runtime startup alone, `-e 0` style: node 22 ms, bun 6 ms, python3 14 ms. Fresh-process RSS with SQLite open and a listener: Node 61 MiB, Bun 18 MiB.

**These numbers are an upper bound on what the plumbing allows, not a KB forecast.** They exclude FTS, Korean tokenizing, bitemporal filters, contract validation and heavy CLI imports. All paths have well over 150 ms of headroom left for those.

### Options

| Option | Fits | Weakness | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **In-process library** | KB in TS, compatible with the gateway runtime | Ties versions and crash domain. A sync query blocks the event loop, MCP streams included. `bun:sqlite` code will not run on Node | **Preferred** if KB is TS. Use a Worker for heavy queries |
| **Long-lived child over stdio** (`kb serve --stdio`) | Any KB language | KB must ship a small loop. Not in the original list | **Preferred** if KB is Python or Rust. Warm handle, no port, no daemon: the gateway starts and reaps it |
| **Per-request CLI spawn** | Any language, simplest contract | Startup cost is unbounded if the CLI imports grow. Spawn storms on facets and polling | **Fallback**. Set a startup budget of about 50 ms in KB CI |
| **Socket-activated KB service** | KB wants HTTP but no daemon | One more unit pair and port, and the KB owns HTTP after all | Works, but adds nothing over the two above while the gateway exists |

Design rule: put a `KbReader` interface in the gateway with one method per contract operation, returning contract JSON. Implementations swap without touching routes. Test every implementation against KB-owned fixtures.

### Constraints this imposes on the KB ADR

- **Storage engine concurrency decides whether a held read handle is safe.**
  - [SQLite WAL](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html): readers and one writer coexist. Handle occasional `SQLITE_BUSY`.
  - [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/connect/concurrency.html): either one read-write process, or many read-only processes with no writer. A gateway holding a read handle would block ingest there, so it must open per request or read a snapshot.
  - Other engines: check the same way before choosing in-process.
- **Query path must be read-only by construction.** Open read-only, since the viewer is read-only by requirement.
- **Version check at startup.** The gateway should compare the contract version with what the library or CLI reports, and fail closed.
- **Overview responses are large.** At 2.1 MB for the synthetic graph, prefer a precomputed or compressed overview. Keep this out of per-request spawn.

## 6. Build order

1. Hono app with `/healthz`, Host/Origin check, static UI, fixture-backed `/api/kb/v1`, and `KbReader` returning KB fixtures. Nothing else depends on the real KB.
2. systemd socket and service units, plus `loginctl enable-linger`.
3. Mount the first MCP server with a bearer token. Verify with Claude Code.
4. Real `KbReader` when the KB ships.
5. Tailscale Serve when another device needs access. Test placement first.
6. Re-decide agentgateway with the MCP track.

## 7. Open questions

1. What language and storage engine does the KB use? This picks library versus stdio child, and decides whether a held read handle is safe.
2. Does the MCP track adopt agentgateway? This decides one process versus two.
3. Does the user want the viewer available with no WSL terminal open? This decides keep-alive level 0 or 1.
4. Is a Claude cloud connector needed? If yes, public exposure and OAuth enter scope.
5. If the KB ships TS on `bun:sqlite`, the gateway runtime conflicts with the Node choice. Resolve this with `node:sqlite` or the proxyd shim, or wait for Bun #44013.

## 8. Not verified

- agentgateway, Caddy, Traefik, Envoy and Pomerium were not run; claims come from docs and source.
- Hono's Node adapter with `listen({fd:3})`, `hono/proxy` SSE passthrough, and Hono MCP mounting on revision 2026-07-28.
- Tailscale placement on WSL. Latency from a Windows browser through mirrored networking.
- Whether Traefik serves static files (prior knowledge says no). Envoy AI Gateway standalone mode.
- Cloudflare free-plan limits and Tailscale pricing.
- Whether Claude Code accepts plain `http://` to loopback with a bearer header was not stated in the section read; expected to work, confirm in step 3.

| Option | Latest release | License | Activity | Runtime, no-Docker | Hosts KB code? | Static UI | MCP aware | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hono** + `@hono/node-server` | hono 4.13.14, 2026-10-25; node-server 2.1.5 | MIT | pushed 2026-10-30 | npm package on Node or Bun, no Docker | **Yes** | Yes | Via `@hono/mcp` 0.3.5 or SDK | **Adopt** |
| **agentgateway** | v1.7.0, 2026-10-27 | Apache-2.0 | pushed 2026-10-30 | Binary, [install script or manual download](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/documentation/setup/install/binary.md); no Docker needed | No | [Not listed in docs](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/llms.txt) | Yes, stdio and OpenAPI targets | **Adapt**, only if MCP track picks it |
| **Caddy** | v2.11.7, 2026-10-03 | Apache-2.0 | pushed 2026-10-30 | Single binary, .deb release assets | No | Yes | No | Reject for now; first choice if a proxy is ever needed |
| **Traefik** | v3.7.17, 2026-10-30 | MIT | pushed 2026-10-30 | Release tarball | No | Not verified | [MCP governance is Hub-only, paid](https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/features/) | Reject |
| **Envoy** | v1.40.2, 2026-10-27 | Apache-2.0 | pushed 2026-10-30 | Not checked | No | No (prior knowledge) | Envoy AI Gateway v1.2.0 is separate; standalone mode not verified | Reject: config cost |
| **Pingora** | 0.9.0, 2026-09-09 | Apache-2.0 | pushed 2026-10-31 | Rust library; you write and compile a proxy. No cargo here | Only by writing Rust | No | No | Reject |
| **River** (Pingora proxy) | v0.5.0, 2024-08-30 | Apache-2.0 | last push 2024-09-06 | Not checked | No | Not checked | No | Reject: dormant |

Metadata comes from the GitHub and npm APIs on 2026-10-31.

Caddy facts, for later use:
- [Flushes `text/event-stream` immediately](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy) and supports unix-socket upstreams.
- Has socket activation through `bind fd/3`. The source confirms the `fd` and `fdgram` networks ([listeners.go](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/master/listeners.go)), and [named sockets merged for v2.11.1](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/7243). The [conventions page](https://caddyserver.com/docs/conventions) does not list them.

agentgateway can mix an MCP route and a plain host route on one listener ([routes doc](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/documentation/configuration/routes.md)). It also has [API key auth](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/documentation/configuration/security/apikey-authn.md), JWT, CORS and access logs. Not verified: whether API keys work with `Authorization: Bearer`, and whether it can accept a systemd-passed socket. Its [MCP auth](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/documentation/mcp/mcp-authn.md) validates tokens from an external authorization server.

### One process or proxy plus MCP gateway

| Layout | Processes | Operating cost | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hono only | 1 | One codebase, one unit pair | Default. MCP servers are few and mounted in-process, or at separate `/mcp/<name>` paths |
| agentgateway → Hono | 2 | One YAML, plus Hono. Front is always on, Hono can stay socket-activated at `host: 127.0.0.1:8788` | MCP track wants tool aggregation or stdio supervision |
| Caddy → Hono | 2 | Caddyfile plus one more binary to update | Only for LAN-wide TLS or several unrelated apps. Tailscale Serve covers TLS |
| Caddy → agentgateway → Hono | 3 | Three configs for one user | Never |

Keep separate `/mcp/<name>` paths until a single merged endpoint is shown to be needed. Claude Code handles several entries natively (`claude mcp add` per path).

### MCP protocol effect on the gateway

- Current revision is [2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning). [Streamable HTTP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/transports/streamable-http) dropped the GET stream and protocol sessions. Each message is one POST.
- This suits idle exit: a restart loses no session state. Older revisions up to 2025-11-25 had `Mcp-Session-Id`, so mount any legacy-era server in stateless mode, or expect session loss on idle exit.
- `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers let an intermediary route or log without parsing bodies.
- `subscriptions/listen` is a long-lived SSE stream. Count open streams as activity in the idle timer. I did not determine whether Claude Code opens one.
- The spec requires `Origin` validation (403 if present and invalid), says local servers should bind to 127.0.0.1, and says servers should authenticate.
- Servers should send `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and periodic `:` SSE comments on long streams.

**Bun pitfall if Bun is used anywhere:** [Bun.serve closes idle connections after 10 s by default](https://bun.com/docs/guides/http/sse), and a quiet SSE stream counts as idle. Use `server.timeout(req, 0)` or set `idleTimeout`. [Field reports](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/27479) put the maximum at 255 s, with 0 disabling it.

## 3. Access and auth

### Reachability

| Mode | Setup | Reachable from | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Localhost** | None. This host already has `networkingMode=Mirrored` in `.wslconfig` | Windows browser, WSL tools | **Adopt now** |
| **Tailscale Serve** | Install Tailscale, then `tailscale serve --bg 8787` | Own tailnet devices only | **Next step** when phone or laptop access is wanted |
| **Cloudflare Tunnel + Access** | Domain on Cloudflare, `cloudflared` | Public internet behind Access | Only if a Claude cloud connector is wanted |

Localhost notes:
- In [mirrored mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/networking) Windows and WSL reach each other over `127.0.0.1`. In NAT mode `localhost` forwarding also works, with [`localhostForwarding` default true](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config).
- Bind `127.0.0.1` explicitly. Microsoft notes `::1` is not supported for Linux reaching Windows; do not assume it the other way either.
- Mirrored mode lets [Windows ports block Linux binds](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config) (see `ignoredPorts`). Pick a quiet port.
- Mirrored mode also allows LAN access once Hyper-V firewall rules are opened. A `127.0.0.1` bind avoids that.

Tailscale Serve notes:
- [Provisions TLS for the tailnet name and adds `Tailscale-User-Login`](https://tailscale.com/kb/1312/serve). It strips client-supplied copies, so a backend bound to localhost can trust the header.
- [`--bg` persists across reboots; `--set-path` maps paths](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/tailscale-cli/serve).
- Serve is config on `tailscaled`, not a process of ours, but `tailscaled` is itself always on.
- Tailscale is not installed in WSL, and not at the default Windows path. I could not confirm from primary sources whether Serve on the Windows host reaches a WSL `127.0.0.1` service in mirrored mode, or whether `tailscaled` inside WSL is the better placement. Test before relying on it.

Cloud connector note:
- [Claude custom connectors connect from Anthropic's cloud](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp), so a tailnet or localhost server fails. [Hostnames resolving to private or CGNAT addresses are rejected](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/troubleshooting).
- Claude Code in WSL has no such limit because it connects locally.
- For public exposure: Cloudflare Access [Managed OAuth](https://blog.cloudflare.com/managed-oauth-for-access) or Anthropic's [MCP tunnels](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/mcp-tunnels/overview) (documented as subject to change).
- [Secure MCP servers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/ai-controls/secure-mcp-servers/) requires a hostname proxied through Cloudflare DNS, and Managed OAuth only for servers that validate the Access JWT.
- Not determined: free-plan seat limits and whether these features are on the free plan.

### What Claude Code requires

From the [Claude Code MCP docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp):
- `--transport http` is the recommended remote transport. SSE is deprecated. WebSocket goes through `add-json`.
- Static auth: `claude mcp add --transport http sagae http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`. With a configured `Authorization` header, Claude Code does not fall back to OAuth.
- `.mcp.json` headers support `${VAR}` expansion. `headersHelper` runs a command per connection and re-runs on 401 or 403.
- OAuth needs RFC 9728 metadata, then RFC 8414. Dynamic registration is the default; pre-configured `--client-id`, `--callback-port` and CIMD are also supported.
- Reconnect: up to 5 attempts mid-session, up to 3 retries on first connection. Connection refused during a WSL restart recovers within that window only if the gateway returns quickly.
- Tool calls abort after 5 minutes of silence on HTTP. Output limit defaults to 25,000 tokens.

[MCP authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/authorization) is optional. So a static bearer token is valid for a personal setup. A public OAuth setup must implement Protected Resource Metadata and audience-bound tokens.

### Auth choice

| Layer | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| All routes | Host and Origin allow-list | Blocks DNS rebinding from any site in the Windows browser. Required for MCP, cheap for the rest |
| `/mcp/*` | Static bearer token via `hono/bearer-auth`, stored in an `EnvironmentFile` mode 600 | Works with Claude Code today with no IdP |
| Viewer UI and APIs, localhost | No login | Read-only, loopback-bound, same-user machine |
| Viewer UI and APIs, Tailscale | Check `Tailscale-User-Login` | Identity for free, no login page |
| **oauth2-proxy** v7.15.5, 2026-10-01, MIT | **Reject for now** | Needs an OIDC provider. Its [`skip_jwt_bearer_tokens`](https://oauth2-proxy.github.io/oauth2-proxy/configuration/overview/) only passes verified JWTs, not static tokens |
| **Pomerium** v0.33.6, 2026-10-27, Apache-2.0 | **Reject for now** | [Linux tarball, no Docker needed, but the sample config expects an IdP](https://www.pomerium.com/docs/deploy/core). Real [MCP gateway features](https://www.pomerium.com/docs/capabilities/mcp) serve multi-user, upstream OAuth cases. Revisit if the setup goes public |

## 4. Lifecycle on WSL2

### Facts that shape the design

- ["systemd services will NOT keep your WSL instance alive."](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/systemd)
- [`[general] instanceIdleTimeout`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config) defaults to 15000 ms; -1 disables it. `[wsl2] vmIdleTimeout` defaults to 60000 ms and is Windows 11 only.
- `wsl --shutdown` stops all distros at once ([wsl-config](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config)).
- [WSL issue 13291](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/13291): `vmIdleTimeout=-1` alone was not enough. The thread's fix sets both keys, and a maintainer edited his message to match.
- Field reports say [a `wsl.exe` client must exist or the distro stops within seconds](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/discussions/9245). Common fix: a logon task running `wsl.exe -d <distro> --exec sleep infinity`, unticking the 3-day task limit.

Observed on this host: systemd on, `Linger=no`, no idle keys in `.wslconfig`, `autoMemoryReclaim=Gradual`, memory cap 48 GB. The installed WSL version was not checked; latest release is 3.0.3 (2026-10-09).

### What happens when

| Event | Result |
|---|---|
| Last WSL client exits | Distro stops after about 15 s by default. Gateway and socket unit die. |
| Viewer tab keeps polling | Inference, not documented: polling does not count as a client, so the tab starts failing. Show an "offline" state. |
| `wsl --shutdown` or Windows reboot | Everything stops. Nothing restarts until something launches WSL. |
| WSL restarts | Enabled socket units come back if the user manager runs, which needs `loginctl enable-linger sagae`. |
| Connection to a stopped WSL | Inference: a socket unit is a listener inside the VM, so nothing is listening and the connection fails. I found no primary statement that a localhost connection boots WSL. Assume it does not. Not tested, because testing from inside WSL requires stopping it. |
| Windows sleep or hibernate | Not researched. |

### Service manager

| Option | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **systemd user units + linger** | **Adopt** | Already running here. Socket activation, restart, journald, no new dependency. Same model in a Proxmox LXC |
| **systemd socket activation** | **Adopt**, via Node | Fits the KB's minimal-always-on principle |
| **pm2** 7.1.1, 2026-10-23 | **Reject** | Its own daemon, and [`pm2 startup` is itself systemd](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/startup/) on this host, so it adds a layer. No socket activation benefit. npm metadata lists AGPL-3.0 |

Sketch:

```ini
# ~/.config/systemd/user/sagae-gateway.socket
[Socket]
ListenStream=127.0.0.1:8787
[Install]
WantedBy=sockets.target

# ~/.config/systemd/user/sagae-gateway.service
[Service]
ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/node %h/sagae-tools/apps/gateway/dist/main.js
EnvironmentFile=%h/.config/sagae-gateway/env
Restart=on-failure
```

```ts
const server = createAdaptorServer({ fetch: app.fetch });
if (process.env.LISTEN_FDS === "1") server.listen({ fd: 3 });
else server.listen(8787, "127.0.0.1");
```

- Idle exit is app code: exit 0 when no request or open stream for N minutes. Set N above the 30-60 s poll, for example 10 minutes. The socket stays armed by systemd.
- With `Accept=no`, [one service handles all connections](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.socket.html).
- Node is under nvm here, so use a stable symlink rather than a versioned path.
- The Hono adapter path was not tested, because nothing third-party could be installed. A bare `node:http` server with `listen({fd:3})` was.

### Bun and socket activation

- Measured on bun 1.4.4: `Bun.serve({fd:3})` logged `3000 localhost` and clients timed out, 10 of 10. It ignored the fd without an error.
- Matches open issues: [#22559](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/22559) and PR [#44013](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/44013).
- Workaround tested: a shell shim starts Bun on a private port and execs [`systemd-socket-proxyd`](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-socket-proxyd.html). 7 of 10 runs took 16-19 ms; 3 took about 1.02 s, cause not diagnosed. It works but adds a moving part.
- Tradeoff: Bun starts faster and uses less memory (below), but Node gives working activation with no shim. Hono keeps the switch to a few lines, so this is reversible once #44013 lands.

### Keep-alive policy

1. **Level 0, default.** No keep-alive. The gateway works whenever a WSL session is open, which matches daily use with Claude Code.
2. **Level 1, if the viewer must work with no terminal.** Set `[general] instanceIdleTimeout=-1` and `[wsl2] vmIdleTimeout=-1`, plus a logon task that boots the distro. Cost: these are global, and the VM stays resident. Weigh this against the KB principle, because it trades one small process for a whole always-on VM.
3. **Level 2, if it must work with the PC off.** Move to a Proxmox LXC.

### Moving to Proxmox LXC later

- Same units, converted to system units with `User=`. Socket activation behaves the same, and a real always-on host removes the WSL problems above.
- Tailscale in LXC: [pass through `/dev/net/tun`](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/containers/lxc/lxc-unprivileged), for example `pct set CTID --dev0 /dev/net/tun`.
- **KB data must move with the gateway when using a local DB.** [SQLite WAL requires all processes on one host and does not work over a network filesystem](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html). If the DB stays in WSL, the KB would then need a network read path.
- Keep the DB on ext4 inside WSL, never under `/mnt/c`.

## 5. KB integration: can the gateway host the read surface?

**Yes.** Measured on a synthetic SQLite graph: 10k nodes, 50k edges, 4.4 MB. A neighbor request returned 200 edges plus nodes, about 69 KB JSON. Client and server were in the same VM with a warm page cache.

| Path | p50 | p95 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-process, `bun:sqlite`, sequential | 1.0 ms | 1.7 ms | n=1000 |
| In-process, 8 concurrent | 3.4 ms | 5.7 ms | n=800 |
| In-process via one extra HTTP hop | 1.5 ms | 2.1 ms | A proxy costs about 0.4 ms |
| Overview dump, all nodes and edges, in-process | 13.6 ms | 20.3 ms | 2.1 MB JSON, n=30. Sync, blocks the event loop |
| Spawn CLI per request, Bun | 9.6 ms | 11.1 ms | n=100 |
| Spawn CLI, Bun, 8 concurrent | 26.0 ms | 40.8 ms | n=200 |
| Spawn CLI per request, Node | 24.9 ms | 28.8 ms | n=100 |
| Spawn CLI per request, Python stdlib | 24.4 ms | 40.8 ms | n=100, no third-party imports |
| Socket-activated Node, first request | about 45 ms (41.7-47.7) | n/a | One cold start, then in-process speed |

Runtime startup alone, `-e 0` style: node 22 ms, bun 6 ms, python3 14 ms. Fresh-process RSS with SQLite open and a listener: Node 61 MiB, Bun 18 MiB.

**These numbers are an upper bound on what the plumbing allows, not a KB forecast.** They exclude FTS, Korean tokenizing, bitemporal filters, contract validation and heavy CLI imports. All paths have well over 150 ms of headroom left for those.

### Options

| Option | Fits | Weakness | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **In-process library** | KB in TS, compatible with the gateway runtime | Ties versions and crash domain. A sync query blocks the event loop, MCP streams included. `bun:sqlite` code will not run on Node | **Preferred** if KB is TS. Use a Worker for heavy queries |
| **Long-lived child over stdio** (`kb serve --stdio`) | Any KB language | KB must ship a small loop. Not in the original list | **Preferred** if KB is Python or Rust. Warm handle, no port, no daemon: the gateway starts and reaps it |
| **Per-request CLI spawn** | Any language, simplest contract | Startup cost is unbounded if the CLI imports grow. Spawn storms on facets and polling | **Fallback**. Set a startup budget of about 50 ms in KB CI |
| **Socket-activated KB service** | KB wants HTTP but no daemon | One more unit pair and port, and the KB owns HTTP after all | Works, but adds nothing over the two above while the gateway exists |

Design rule: put a `KbReader` interface in the gateway with one method per contract operation, returning contract JSON. Implementations swap without touching routes. Test every implementation against KB-owned fixtures.

### Constraints this imposes on the KB ADR

- **Storage engine concurrency decides whether a held read handle is safe.**
  - [SQLite WAL](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html): readers and one writer coexist. Handle occasional `SQLITE_BUSY`.
  - [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/connect/concurrency.html): either one read-write process, or many read-only processes with no writer. A gateway holding a read handle would block ingest there, so it must open per request or read a snapshot.
  - Other engines: check the same way before choosing in-process.
- **Query path must be read-only by construction.** Open read-only, since the viewer is read-only by requirement.
- **Version check at startup.** The gateway should compare the contract version with what the library or CLI reports, and fail closed.
- **Overview responses are large.** At 2.1 MB for the synthetic graph, prefer a precomputed or compressed overview. Keep this out of per-request spawn.

## 6. Build order

1. Hono app with `/healthz`, Host/Origin check, static UI, fixture-backed `/api/kb/v1`, and `KbReader` returning KB fixtures. Nothing else depends on the real KB.
2. systemd socket and service units, plus `loginctl enable-linger`.
3. Mount the first MCP server with a bearer token. Verify with Claude Code.
4. Real `KbReader` when the KB ships.
5. Tailscale Serve when another device needs access. Test placement first.
6. Re-decide agentgateway with the MCP track.

## 7. Open questions

1. What language and storage engine does the KB use? This picks library versus stdio child, and decides whether a held read handle is safe.
2. Does the MCP track adopt agentgateway? This decides one process versus two.
3. Does the user want the viewer available with no WSL terminal open? This decides keep-alive level 0 or 1.
4. Is a Claude cloud connector needed? If yes, public exposure and OAuth enter scope.
5. If the KB ships TS on `bun:sqlite`, the gateway runtime conflicts with the Node choice. Resolve this with `node:sqlite` or the proxyd shim, or wait for Bun #44013.

## 8. Not verified

- agentgateway, Caddy, Traefik, Envoy and Pomerium were not run; claims come from docs and source.
- Hono's Node adapter with `listen({fd:3})`, `hono/proxy` SSE passthrough, and Hono MCP mounting on revision 2026-07-28.
- Tailscale placement on WSL. Latency from a Windows browser through mirrored networking.
- Whether Traefik serves static files (prior knowledge says no). Envoy AI Gateway standalone mode.
- Cloudflare free-plan limits and Tailscale pricing.
- Whether Claude Code accepts plain `http://` to loopback with a bearer header was not stated in the section read; expected to work, confirm in step 3.

# MCP gateways and aggregators: research report

Date: 2026-10-31. Track: MCP gateways and aggregators for sagae-tools (solo developer, WSL2, no Docker).

Evidence labels:
- **[doc]** the project's docs, README or release notes
- **[src]** I read the source on the default branch through the GitHub API
- **[meta]** GitHub, npm or PyPI metadata
- **[vendor]** the vendor's own marketing claim, not independently checked
- **[inference]** my reasoning, not a stated fact

Nothing was installed or executed. **No memory figure in this report is measured.** I found no published idle RSS for any candidate, so that criterion stays open until a measuring stage.

---

## 1. Bottom line

- **Primary: agentgateway v1.7.0.** It is the only candidate that does both jobs in one no-Docker binary: MCP aggregation and ordinary HTTP routing.
- **Fallback: 1MCP v0.39.7 for MCP, plus Caddy v2.11.7 for HTTP.** No other no-Docker candidate does ordinary HTTP routing, so the fallback has to be two pieces.
- **Custom gateway: not justified.** Section 7 lists each gap found. All have a configuration or small-tool answer that is cheaper than owning a protocol translator.
- **The gateway does not remove the KB's process question.** agentgateway only routes. It cannot host KB read logic, so a KB read API remains a process somewhere. Section 6 gives ways to keep that process on-demand.

Three things to know before adopting agentgateway:

1. Its OpenAPI-to-MCP target cannot read OpenAPI 3.1, and the KB contract is 3.1.
2. It spawns stdio children per session, for every target that passes the condition. Nothing is pooled.
3. It has no tool-search feature. Claude Code's built-in tool search covers this for Claude Code only.

---

## 2. MCP specification as of October 2026

**Current revision: `2026-07-28`** ([versioning](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning), [release tag](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification/releases/tag/2026-07-28)). The [draft changelog](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/changelog) has no entries yet. The prior revision is `2025-11-25`.

### What changed ([changelog](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog))

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Statelessness | `initialize` handshake and `Mcp-Session-Id` removed. Each request carries version and client capabilities in `_meta`. `tools/list` and similar no longer vary per connection. |
| Discovery | New mandatory `server/discover`. Mismatch returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` (-32022). |
| Transport | HTTP GET stream and `resources/subscribe` replaced by `subscriptions/listen`. SSE resumability (`Last-Event-ID`) removed; a broken stream loses the in-flight request. |
| Server-to-client | Server-initiated requests replaced by Multi Round-Trip Requests: `InputRequiredResult`, then a client retry with `inputResponses`. All results carry a required `resultType`. |
| Tasks | Moved out of core into extension `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`. `tasks/result` replaced by polling `tasks/get` plus `tasks/update`. |
| Extensions | `extensions` field added to client and server capabilities. MCP Apps is `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`. |
| Routing headers | `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` required on POST. `x-mcp-header` mirrors tool params into `Mcp-Param-*`. |
| Caching | `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` required on list results and `resources/read`. Deterministic `tools/list` order is a SHOULD. |
| Schema | `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` loosened to any JSON Schema 2020-12 keyword. |
| Auth | Dynamic Client Registration deprecated in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents. `iss` validation (RFC 9207). Credentials keyed by issuer. |
| Deprecated | Roots, Sampling, Logging, HTTP+SSE transport. Minimum window twelve months. |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry trace context conventions documented for `_meta`. |

### Ecosystem position

- Tier 1 SDKs ship the revision. Latest seen: TypeScript `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.4.0 (2026-10-23), Python `mcp` 2.3.0 (2026-10-02). [meta] ([TS releases](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases))
- Claude Code handles the new revision, with visible edges. Changelog 2.1.302 fixes servers that negotiate `2026-07-28` but omit `resultType`, `ttlMs` or `cacheScope` ([changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)). Open issues: [Tasks extension unsupported](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/102347), [`allOf`/`if`/`then` root schemas dropped](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/95504).
- Roadmap ([post](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/mcp-roadmap/)): extend the Streamable HTTP model to local servers, including over stdio. Server Card `.well-known` metadata is still in progress. Expect another transport shift on the stdio side.

### What this means for a gateway

- **Dual-era is mandatory.** The [compatibility matrix](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning) shows modern-to-legacy and legacy-to-modern both fail without a dual-era party. A gateway is the natural translator. A legacy-only gateway only works while clients keep falling back.
- **Parsing the body is required.** Any server that processes the body MUST validate headers against it (-32020). Intermediaries acting on headers SHOULD reject versions that do not require validation ([transport](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http)). A plain reverse proxy can pass MCP through but cannot safely aggregate or filter it.
- **Prefixing has a new cost.** [inference] A gateway that renames tools must rewrite the body and `Mcp-Name` together.
- **Non-ASCII names use a Base64 sentinel in `Mcp-Name`.** This applies directly to Korean resource URIs from the KB, so it needs a smoke test.
- **Sessions go away for modern pairs, so no session store is needed in principle.** Legacy clients and servers still need sessions, so gateways keep both paths.
- **Three relays are easy to miss:** `subscriptions/listen` fan-out, `input_required` retries, and task handles. [Bifrost currently fails `input_required`](https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/issues/9241) on upstream calls.
- **Merged lists need a defensible `ttlMs` and `cacheScope`.** With per-client filtering the scope must be `private`. [inference]
- **Local servers still need `Origin` validation and loopback binding.** Both come from the transport's Security section.

---
