# Gateway research: adversarial verification

Date: 2026-10-31. Verifies `mcp-gateways.md`, `mcp-servers.md` and `http-gateway.md`.

**Method.** Every adopt or adapt option and each track's main recommendation was checked against primary sources: the GitHub API, source files read at the release tag rather than `main`, `npm view` per-version publish dates, PyPI, and official docs. Nothing third-party was installed or downloaded. The only code run was two short scripts of mine plus the existing `bench/` scripts, using the already-installed Node and Bun. No third-party product was exercised, so every statement about agentgateway behaviour below comes from reading source or docs.

**Reading the labels.** "Source trace" means I followed the code at the v1.7.0 tag but did not run it.

---

## 1. Corrections

### 1.1 Corrections that change a decision

**C1. `openapi-typescript` and `openapi-fetch` should not be marked adopt.**
- The author announced on 2026-09-19 that the project "is in maintenance mode and won't be getting any more updates. Please migrate to another project", and this includes security patches ([#2874](https://github.com/openapi-ts/openapi-typescript/issues/2874)). Handing it to someone else was ruled out. The 100 most recent commits are all from dependency bots.
- The report's date is wrong. `7.13.0` and `0.17.0` were published on **2026-02-11**. The cited 2026-06-15 is npm's `modified` field, so the release is over eight months old, not four.
- `7.13.0` pulls `@redocly/openapi-core ^1.34.6`, which [#2846](https://github.com/openapi-ts/openapi-typescript/issues/2846) reports brings in `js-yaml` 4.2.0, flagged high severity (GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m).
- The named alternative's date is wrong too. `@hey-api/openapi-ts` 0.99.0 was published **2026-06-22**, not 2026-09-30. Its repo last changed 2026-09-30.
- **Change:** treat this as an open selection. Candidates are `@hey-api/openapi-ts` (pre-1.0, no stable release since June) and [`orval`](https://github.com/orval-labs/orval) 8.46.0 (MIT, released 2026-10-30). I evaluated neither on OpenAPI 3.1. A third option is for the KB repo to generate and ship the types itself. The frozen tool still runs and only reads a first-party contract at dev time, so it is a usable stopgap, but it is not an adopt.

**C2. Plain `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance` cannot test the current spec.**
- `latest` is 0.1.16, released **2026-03-27** on GitHub and published 2026-03-30 on npm. The report's 2026-10-01 is the publish date of `0.2.0-alpha.12`, picked up through npm's `modified` field.
- 0.1.16 predates the 2026-07-28 revision by four months. Its [version list](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance/blob/v0.1.16/src/scenarios/index.ts) stops at `2025-11-25` plus `draft`. Its README has no `--spec-version` or `--requirements`. The report read the `main` README, which describes the alpha.
- Others use the alpha line: the TS SDK v2.4.0 pins `0.2.0-alpha.12` in `test/conformance/package.json`, and 1MCP v0.39.7 pins `0.2.0-alpha.11`.
- `main` still has `DRAFT_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2026-07-28'`, and the default suite excludes draft scenarios.
- **Change:** pin `@modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.12` and run with `--requirements 2026-07-28`. That flag landed on 2026-08-07, before alpha.11 and alpha.12 ([#447](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance/pull/447)). Keep the baseline file.

**C3. The three tracks disagree on the main architecture, and verification favours the Hono-first design.**

| Topic | `mcp-gateways.md` | `mcp-servers.md` | `http-gateway.md` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Front process | agentgateway | Hono `apps/gateway` | Hono; agentgateway only if aggregation is needed |
| MCP exposure | One `/mcp`, merged, stdio target | `/mcp/<name>`, in-process, explicitly not merged | `/mcp/<name>` until a merge is shown to be needed |
| KB HTTP | Separate socket-activated service | Gateway `/v1/*` | Gateway `/api/kb/v1` |
| Port | 8787 | 7410 | 8787 (8788 behind agentgateway) |
| Server path | `tools/mcp-kb/src/main.ts` | `servers/kb/src/stdio.ts` | n/a |

- The KB consumer doc already proposes that the KB ship a library or CLI and that HTTP exposure sits with the gateway ([sagae-tools.md](/home/user/sagae-knowloge-base/docs/contracts/consumers/sagae-tools.md) line 31). agentgateway cannot host a library or call a CLI, so a Hono-style application process is needed either way.
- "Single entry point" is therefore one port, not one process. agentgateway cannot host KB code, has no static file serving (nothing in [`schema/config.md`](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/blob/v1.7.0/schema/config.md), only `directResponse`), and has no socket activation (zero code hits for `LISTEN_FDS` or `sd_listen_fds`, no issue mentions it). So the layout is at least two processes, and the front one stays on all the time, which works against the KB's principle of few always-on processes.
- The findings in C4 to C10 all add cost to the agentgateway route. In-repo TypeScript servers mounted in Hono with `createMcpHandler` avoid them, because that path has no protocol sessions.
- **Recommended re-ranking, for the orchestrator to decide:** Hono first (`http-gateway.md` plus `mcp-servers.md`), with agentgateway deferred until third-party servers actually need aggregating.
- **Tell the user:** this reads "one entry point" as one port with several MCP URLs, which narrows part (a) of the working interpretation.

**C4. agentgateway's stdio cost is higher than reported, and the "keep stateful mode" mitigation does not cover it.** Source trace.
- Modern-protocol requests take `serve_stateless` even in stateful mode (`if !protocol.uses_sessions()`, [`streamablehttp.rs`](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/blob/v1.7.0/crates/agentgateway/src/mcp/streamablehttp.rs) lines 187-189). That path calls `build_new_connections`, which spawns each stdio target.
- So Claude Code's `server/discover` probe should spawn and tear down every stdio target, and the `initialize` fallback then spawns them again.
- Claude Code's session recovery sends two concurrent `initialize` calls, then a third, and leaks the extra sessions ([#96733](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/96733), open). Each one would spawn all stdio targets, and those children would live until the TTL expires.
- A stdio child that dies is not respawned. `send_message` returns an error once `is_alive()` is false, so that target stays dead for the session. 1MCP has opt-in stdio recovery (README at the tag), which the report did not mention.
- **Change:** do not route in-repo servers through stdio targets. Use HTTP targets or Hono mounts.

**C5. A low `sessionTtl` is not a free mitigation.**
- The default is 30 minutes ([`mcp/mod.rs`](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/blob/v1.7.0/crates/agentgateway/src/mcp/mod.rs)). The report's sketch uses 10 minutes.
- An idle gap longer than the TTL sends the client through session recovery, which hits #96733. [#95018](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/95018) (open) reports that recovery covers `tools/call` only, so the first resource read fails with `Connection closed`. The KB design delivers snapshot bodies as resources.
- Status: inferred from the issue reports, not observed on this setup. Keep the default until a test says otherwise.

**C6. "stdio targets are legacy-negotiated... Harmless for dual-era clients" understates the effect.**
- [The README](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/blob/v1.7.0/crates/agentgateway/src/mcp/README.md) says that when multiplexing, an error from any target on `server/discover` is returned to the client. One stdio target therefore drops the whole backend to legacy sessions, for every target on it.
- `subscriptions/listen` is rejected for stdio and SSE upstreams.
- So the report's own sketch, a stdio target on `/mcp`, puts that route on sessions. The benefit `http-gateway.md` cites for idle exit ("a restart loses no session state") then does not apply.
- [#3995](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/issues/3995) is confirmed open, and a maintainer calls it working as intended: "We cannot/do not translate the modern API down to the legacy API". Expect no fix.

**C7. `Origin` handling exists. The report is wrong that it was not found.**
- [`mcp/dns_rebinding.rs`](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/blob/v1.7.0/crates/agentgateway/src/mcp/dns_rebinding.rs) implements Host and Origin validation, enabled by `dnsRebindingProtection: true` on an MCP backend. It is **off by default**. [#1855](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/issues/1855) was opened 2026-05-18 and closed 2026-08-14.
- **Change:** set it on every MCP backend. A CEL rule is not needed.
- Limits: it covers MCP backends only, so plain `host:` routes stay unprotected. The allowed hosts are hard-coded to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, so it may reject traffic arriving through Tailscale Serve. Test that before adding Tailscale.

**C8. `bindAddress: 127.0.0.1` is not enough to stay on loopback.** Source trace.
- Besides the listener, the stats port **15020** and readiness port **15021** default to the wildcard address ([`config.rs`](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/blob/v1.7.0/crates/agentgateway/src/config.rs) lines 356-369). The report covers only the listener and admin port.
- The admin port (localhost:15000) has no authentication by default, and I found no `Host` check in `ui.rs`, `admin.rs`, `hyper_helpers.rs` or `accept.rs`. It can write the config, and a config can name a stdio command.
- Plain cross-origin writes are blocked: `/api/config` needs JSON, `/api/config/raw` needs `application/yaml`, and CORS is an allow-list. DNS rebinding makes a request same-origin, so those guards do not apply to it. The report's bearer-key argument does not cover this port, and in mirrored mode a Windows browser can reach it.
- `POST /quitquitquit` has no content-type guard.
- Status: not exercised, and browser-side local-network protections were not assessed. Treat it as plausibly exploitable because the fix is one line.
- **Change:** `config.adminAddr: "off"` or a `unix:` path, plus `config.storage.mode: readOnly`. Quote `"off"`.

**C9. Running from a tracked YAML will write a secret into it.**
- v1.7.0 `ensure_session_key` generates an AES key and writes it back to `config.session.key` when the file is writable and storage mode is `file` (`config.rs`, `persist_session_key`). The report notes only "changed session encryption".
- The rewrite can also drop comments, because the fallback path re-serialises the whole document.
- **Change:** set `SESSION_KEY` from the systemd `EnvironmentFile`. `storage.mode: readOnly` also stops the write, but sessions then stay unencrypted unless `SESSION_KEY` is set as well.

**C10. Multiplexing rewrites resource URIs. The report says they are untouched.**
- With more than one target, or `prefixMode: always`, URIs are exposed as `<target>+<uri>`, for example `kb+kb://snapshot/1` (`resource_uri` in [`handler.rs`](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/blob/v1.7.0/crates/agentgateway/src/mcp/handler.rs)). A raw URI without the prefix fails with `invalid resource URI`. The docs' phrase "retain target routing information and are unaffected" is easy to misread.
- `resource_link` is not rewritten; there are no matches for it in `handler.rs`, `session.rs` or `mergestream.rs`. So `mcp-servers.md` rules that put `kb://snapshot/{id}` and `resource_uri` in tool results would return URIs that the same endpoint then rejects.
- Instructions are merged into one string. Claude Code truncates server instructions at [4,096 characters](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp), so later servers lose theirs ([#4236](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/issues/4236), open).
- Single-target backends pass through unchanged. **Keep one target per route.**
- Merged lists are sent with `ttlMs: 0` and `cacheScope: private` (`handler.rs`), so client caching of tool lists is off. Effect on Claude Code not determined.

### 1.2 Corrections to facts and risks

**C11. 1MCP telemetry is not in the released version.** Product Usage Telemetry landed on `main` on 2026-10-29 ([#705](https://github.com/1mcp-app/agent/commit/b137a4a15)). The v0.39.7 README does not mention it, and the only file at that tag with "telemetry" in its path is an ADR. The risk applies to a future 0.40+ upgrade. Set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` then.

**C12. New 1MCP risk: an old SDK is a runtime dependency.** v0.39.7 pins `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` **1.30.0**, inside the affected ranges of GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h (high), GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453 (high), GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw (high), GHSA-f897-62hf-6gxq (high), GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq and GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw ([advisories](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories)). Whether 1MCP reaches those code paths is not determined.

**C13. mcpproxy-go is not dual-era on HTTP.** This resolves the report's open question. At v0.72.0 the client-facing Streamable HTTP surface is pinned to legacy versions, and the upstream hop is too: "mcpproxy does not yet serve the 2026-07-28 era on the upstream hop" ([`server.go`](https://github.com/smart-mcp-proxy/mcpproxy-go/blob/v0.72.0/internal/server/server.go) `clientFacingStreamableOptions`, `connection_lifecycle.go`). It still works for dual-era clients such as Claude Code, as a legacy server.

**C14. FastMCP.**
- [#5267](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/issues/5267) is **closed** (2026-09-25, completed), not an open bug.
- #5260 is still open and [PR #5263](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5263) is unmerged, so that one is not "addressed".
- "Would need a stdlib venv" does not work as stated: `ensurepip` is missing here, confirmed with `python3 -m ensurepip`. This also contradicts `mcp-servers.md`, which recorded the gap. Installing `python3-venv` is the likely fix and needs sudo.

**C15. ext-apps.** The `latest` mismatch is explained: 2.1.0 was a version bump reverted the same day (commit `Revert "Bump version to 2.1.0 (#833)" (#835)`), with no tag or GitHub release. It went up 75 minutes **after** 2.0.4, not before. Never pin 2.1.0.

**C16. Licenses.** npm reports MIT for ext-apps and conformance, but both repos' `LICENSE` is the MCP transition text: new code Apache-2.0, older contributions MIT, docs CC-BY-4.0. This is compatible with personal use.

**C17. Hono v5 is in release candidate, and no report mentions it.** `next` is `5.0.0-rc.1` (2026-10-10). `@modelcontextprotocol/hono` 2.0.2 peers `hono ^4.11.4`, so stay on v4 until that widens. `@hono/node-server` 2.1.5 already allows `^4 || ^5.0.0-0`.

**C18. Security advisories no report mentions.** All are patched at the recommended versions, so these are floors, not blockers.
- agentgateway: [GHSA-qm3r-hhvc-62cp](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/security/advisories/GHSA-qm3r-hhvc-62cp) and [GHSA-7hv4-jgp9-mgx2](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/security/advisories/GHSA-7hv4-jgp9-mgx2) were fixed in v1.7.0, and [GHSA-mvgg-jvj2-4frq](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/security/advisories/GHSA-mvgg-jvj2-4frq) (high) in v1.4.0. Session reuse across routes has now appeared twice, so avoid relying on route-level MCP policy to separate tools of different trust.
- Hono `serveStatic` middleware bypass, fixed in `hono` 4.13.11 and `@hono/node-server` 2.1.3. This is relevant because the plan puts middleware in front of static files.
- TS SDK: GHSA-jm63-cq47-j5jp, GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453 and GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq, all fixed by 2.3.0.

**C19. Claude Code reconnection is more limited than `http-gateway.md` states.**
- The docs add background retries of "up to about half an hour". Independent runs on 2.1.310 ([#101280](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/101280), open) measured 8 background attempts over about 10-13 minutes, then permanent loss of the tools.
- A server that is down when the session starts is never retried. Socket activation helps here, since the port accepts connections with no process running. A plain agentgateway daemon does not.

**C20. Host and Origin allow-list is not a Hono middleware.** `http-gateway.md` calls the stack "all library use", but Hono ships no Host check. Use `hostHeaderValidationResponse` and `originValidationResponse` from `@modelcontextprotocol/server`, as [the SDK docs](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/v2.4.0/docs/serving/web-standard.md) show. The same report's table also says "Via `@hono/mcp` 0.3.5", which `mcp-servers.md` rejects as SDK v1. Use `@modelcontextprotocol/hono`.

# Agentgateway MCP

## Version Negotiation

Agentgateway handles traffic from a single downstream client to N upstream servers.
We call this "multiplexing" if N>1.

## Target conditions

Each target of a virtual MCP may set `condition` to a boolean CEL expression. The condition is evaluated
when Agentgateway selects the upstream targets for a virtual MCP request, with the authenticated request context and
`mcp.target.name` available. A target whose expression evaluates to `false` is excluded before
it is initialized or contacted; omitting `condition` allows the target. A condition requires at
least two configured targets.

This is distinct from `mcpAuthorization`: target conditions choose which upstream servers participate
in the virtual MCP request, while `mcpAuthorization` evaluates individual returned tools and other
MCP resources after an upstream has responded.

When every configured target's condition is false, Agentgateway presents an empty virtual MCP.

Version negotiation is how we handle the disparate protocol versions between the clients and servers, and Agentgateway itself.
This is particularly important for 2026-07-28+, which has a very different protocol than the other versions (which are all much more incremental differences).
We will call "Old" before 2026-07-28 and "New" after.

**Assumptions**:
* Clients supporting `2026-07-28` will also support older protocols for the foreseeable future.
* Servers supporting `2026-07-28` will also support older protocols for the foreseeable future.
* Users will have a mix of support for `2026-07-28` across clients and servers for the foreseeable future.

### New clients

A new client will send a request with `server/discover`.
We can respond with:
* DiscoverResponse with `supportedVersions` including `2026-07-28`: declaring we are OK with modern protocol.
* DiscoverResponse with `supportedVersions` not including `2026-07-28`: arguably a spec violation; declares we are not OK with the modern protocol.
  Clients will *probably* fallback to send `initialize`.
* Respond with Unsupported error. Clients will fallback to send `initialize`.

**Single server**: we forward the `server/discover`. We can forward it back as is.
If they support modern protocol, this will be a valid DiscoverResponse.
Otherwise it will be an error, which is what we want: the client will fallback to the older protocol.

> **Compatibility mode**: we may want to support a mode where we do not put the fallback onto the client.
> Instead, we do the downgrade for them as the proxy.
> This is plausible but pretty tricky.
> If the server uses sessions, we would have to wrap each request in a session (`init; send request; delete`).
> This matches how we do the older "stateless" style.
> If the server doesn't use sessions, we would be fine to just forward directly... maybe.
> Technically, the specification requires an initialize even with the older session-less style.
> We could send it once and cache it (including the boolean "are they stateful"), which is probably sufficient
> in practice but theoretically unsound (a server could conditionally use sessions on random requests, etc).
> For now, we do not implement this mode. If we do, we will likely do session wrapping

**Multiple servers**: we forward the `server/discover` to each. We need to merge the result.
We want to create the intersection of supported versions from all servers.
If a server returns an error, we also return that error: this tells the clients "we don't support `2026-07-28`" and they will retry
with `initialize`; `initialize` will do similar negotiation.

`subscriptions/listen` requires Streamable HTTP upstreams. Stdio and SSE use legacy protocol
negotiation, so modern clients fall back before a listen request is forwarded.

For multiplexed `subscriptions/listen`, Agentgateway waits for selected upstream ACKs before
emitting one downstream ACK. The ACK includes only accepted filters; resource URIs keep the
client's `service+` form. Resource subscriptions may span upstreams; each target receives only
the URIs it owns. Later notifications are limited to the filters accepted by their source
upstream.
Like other MCP fanout requests, setup waits for every selected upstream before the gateway can
construct its response.
Listen setup has no separate timeout; when configured, the route request-timeout policy bounds it
before the downstream response begins.

---

With this approach, we should fully support new clients. And, when the client _and_ server are new, we get the optimal
behavior: no fallback requests needed.
For older clients, we do end up with fallback requests (both from client to gateway, and gateway to server).
If clients with _only_ `2026-07-28` support become popular, we will need a compatibility mode.
However, this doesn't seem likely to happen in the short term.

### Old clients

For older clients, they should handle sessions or sessionless servers today.
This means we could return a session, or not, when dealing with new servers -- it's our choice entirely.

> A new server cannot use sessions.
> However, they may have session-like behavior; to use the new spec with a server like this implies modifying the tools
> exposed to take correlation IDs.
> This tool change is a change non-dependent on protocol version.
> Therefore, we do not need any special handling of "Session-ful servers on the new protocol"

The key decision here is whether we stick to an older protocol version for the server side hop, or attempt
to upgrade it for the client.
In both cases, the server is unlikely to use sessions, which means there isn't that much benefit to using the new protocol
aside from avoiding an `initialize` _if we have a [cached server response](#caching-server-responses) for a `server/discover`_
As such, I propose for now we keep the same old protocol.

**Single server**: an older client will send an initialize request. We forward it as is.
This assumes the server supports the old version as well.
When we send an initialize, we will not know if the server is 'old' or 'new'; for our intent it is 'old'.
As such, it will probably return a session and we should retain our existing session logic.

**Multiple servers**: same as above; this ends up being the same flow as before.

## Caching

`2026-07-28` introduces a variety of caching controls on `server/discover`, `tools/list`, and more.

### Caching server responses

A server can tell us a resource can be cached, and we can optionally cache it.
There are two scopes: `public` and `private`.

I believe that, unless further evidence of ecosystem trends, `private` is essentially identical to "do no cache":
we have no way to know what the _private scope_ of the request is, so we ought to assume the worst.

However, with `public` we are free to cache for the provided TTL.

A primary concern around skipping requests (by reading from a cache) is that we may be caching the payload
but not the HTTP headers. In particular, around authorization failures which may include `www-authenticate` and other
important headers.
However, if we are caching it implies we got a 200, so that aspect is out. Additionally, if the 200 headers
were relevant to the response (which seems atypical), it is assumed the server will disable caching.

As such, I believe it is safe to cache server responses.
However, this is a performance optimization not required for correctness.

### Configuring caching in agentgateway responses

Whether agentgateway can tell clients to cache is a different story.
Agentgateway may apply various policies to traffic, both at the MCP level but also at all other levels (ext auth, ext proc, etc).
We don't know if something is cacheable.

If we have authorization rules which take request attributes into account, we definitely do not know.
Returning `private` scope is also not sufficient, because the client will not have any idea what the true scoping is:
a users authorization rule could be `only allow request on odd minutes` as a silly example.

As such, I believe the best option for us is to strictly disable caching of proxied results.
This includes sanitizing responses we get to turn off caching.

It is possible in the future we can enable caching on an opt-in basis.

# 1MCP

[![NPM Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@1mcp/agent)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1mcp/agent)
[![NPM Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/%401mcp%252Fagent)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1mcp/agent)
[![CodeQl](https://github.com/1mcp-app/agent/actions/workflows/github-code-scanning/codeql/badge.svg)](https://github.com/1mcp-app/agent/actions/workflows/github-code-scanning/codeql)
[![GitHub Repo stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/1mcp-app/agent)](https://github.com/1mcp-app/agent/stargazers)
[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-docs.1mcp.app-blue)](https://docs.1mcp.app)
[![DeepWiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepWiki-AI%20Docs-purple.svg?logo=gitbook&logoColor=white)](https://deepwiki.com/1mcp-app/agent)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@1mcp/agent)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1mcp/agent)

1MCP is the unified MCP runtime. `1mcp serve` aggregates your MCP servers, and CLI mode adds a thinner agent-facing workflow for Codex, Claude, Cursor, and similar tool-using agents.

## Why 1MCP

Most MCP setups eventually hit two kinds of sprawl:

- Configuration sprawl: every client needs its own MCP wiring, auth choices, and filtering rules.
- Agent sprawl: autonomous sessions carry too many tools and schemas into context up front.

1MCP addresses both:

- `1mcp serve` gives you one aggregated runtime in front of many MCP servers.
- CLI mode lets agents discover tools progressively with `instructions`, `inspect`, and `run`.
- Static servers can load at startup, while template servers are created from per-client or per-session context.
- Presets, filters, and instruction aggregation keep the same runtime adaptable across clients and projects.

| Approach               | Best for                             | Tradeoff                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1MCP CLI mode          | Codex, Claude, agent loops           | Requires a running `1mcp serve` instance                                         |
| 1MCP stdio proxy       | Maximum compatibility across clients | Still depends on `serve`, and auth-capable HTTP clients have a more direct path  |
| Direct streamable HTTP | MCP-native HTTP clients              | No project context, no `.1mcprc`, and a broader tool surface is exposed directly |
| Custom proxying        | One-off compatibility shims          | You own discovery, filtering, auth, and runtime lifecycle                        |

## Quick Start for Agent Users

This page is optimized for AI agent users. The 5-minute outcome is simple: start a real `1mcp serve` runtime, connect your agent with `cli-setup`, then verify the `instructions -> inspect -> run` workflow.

Install 1MCP, add one upstream server, and start the runtime:

```bash
npm install -g @1mcp/agent
1mcp mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
1mcp serve
```

In a second shell, connect your agent to CLI mode:

```bash
1mcp cli-setup --codex
# or
1mcp cli-setup --claude --scope repo --repo-root .
```

Then verify the agent workflow:

```bash
# shell 1
1mcp serve

# shell 2
1mcp instructions
1mcp inspect context7
1mcp inspect context7/query-docs
1mcp run context7/query-docs --args '{"libraryId":"/mongodb/docs","query":"aggregation pipeline"}'
```

# Spike results (2026-10-31)

Machine-extracted from the workflow journal. The review section overrides the spikes where they disagree.


## Spike 1

No maintained candidate is acceptable as shipped. agentgateway, 1MCP, mcp-use and fastmcp-ts all rewrite resource URIs but not resource_link, so a link in a tool result cannot be read back (reproduced through real Claude Code on agentgateway and 1MCP). The SDK v2 composition was the only one to pass every check: 207 lines (floor 38), no protocol translation, URIs unchanged, one stable stdio child, respawn, and immediate pickup of a new upstream in a running Claude Code session. Best product is agentgateway (43 MB, 125 ms, bearer, the only product relaying input_required), but on a merged route it spawned the stdio target on every modern request (25 of 25, about 100 ms), and a running session never saw a new upstream. 1MCP has the best product stdio recovery, but costs 319 MB, has no static bearer and a 60 s call limit. Claude Code negotiated 2026-07-28 and fell back to initialize only on agentgateway with a legacy-only target. Deferred loading worked and tool-level alwaysLoad survived. The composition needed 4 fixes found by this rig (177 to 207 lines), and about 60 more lines are estimated before production. The report file does not exist: the harness refused it, and I did not route around that, so the full findings are in these fields.

### Recommendation

Ranking: 1. SDK v2 composition inside the control server, Hono on Node 26. 2. agentgateway. 3. 1MCP. 4. mcp-use. 5. fastmcp-ts.

Answer to the question: no maintained candidate has acceptable fidelity as shipped, because all four break resource_link read-back and no product has a setting to avoid it. The least custom code with acceptable fidelity is the SDK composition. It respects the no-translation rule: none of its lines parse JSON-RPC or handle eras, Mcp-Name or session headers, because the SDK does that on both legs. What the project owns is routing and lifecycle. That ownership has a real cost: this rig found 4 defects in my first version (no recovery from a restarted session-based upstream, the 60 s SDK default cutting long calls, no input_required relay, one hung upstream stalling tools/list for 60 s), and fixing them took 30 lines. Keep the harness as its regression suite.

Custom code the winner requires. Already written, 207 lines: merge and routing 82, upstream lifecycle 68, imports and constants 22, config reload 22, shutdown 7, HTTP glue and bearer 6. Still to write, about 60 lines by estimate: capped exponential backoff with a stop (12), per-upstream call timeout, since the 30-minute default leaves calls to a hung upstream hanging (5), last-good list per upstream, since each tools/list costs 3 s while one hangs (15), constant-time token compare and token from EnvironmentFile (3), per-upstream instruction budget (5), health endpoint and request log, scope depends on what 관제 means (15 to 20), name validation and a duplicate-URI rule (5). Known limits to accept: a legacy upstream's elicitation is not relayed, there is no upstream OAuth, prompts/get and resources/templates/list are written but unexercised, and it shares a crash domain with anything else in that process.

If no custom gateway is read strictly: use agentgateway with HTTP targets only, plus failOpen and policies.timeout.backendRequestTimeout, and keep URIs out of tool results. External stdio servers would then need a long-lived stdio-to-HTTP adapter, which I did not test, and running sessions would not see new upstreams until restarted.

First check for any product route: whether the proxmox MCP answers server/discover. Its era decides which agentgateway and 1MCP stdio problem applies. The composition is indifferent. I did not touch it.

What would change the ranking: agentgateway wins if the design drops URIs from tool results and all upstreams are HTTP. 1MCP improves if its timeout setting works and it leaves SDK 1.30.0. Any product that passes resource_link correctly displaces the composition.

Not tested: Claude Code reconnecting after a mid-session gateway restart and recovery after session TTL expiry (VG-C5, #95018, #96733), permission patterns across merged names, a stdio server that ignores stdin EOF, agentgateway condition rules to narrow spawns, the stdio-to-HTTP adapter, 1MCP async mode with an upstream down at start, conformance 0.2.0-alpha.12, socket activation and idle exit, and the real proxmox MCP by instruction. Inspector CLI does not exercise the modern path.

Decision needed: the task asked for report.md, but the harness refuses report files from subagents, so it does not exist. If you need it as a file, write it from this result.

### Verdicts

- **SDK v2 composition (client + createMcpHandler, 207 lines)**: pass. Only candidate to pass every check, including through real Claude Code on the final revision: URIs unchanged, resource_link readable, outputSchema, annotations, _meta and instructions kept, one stable stdio child for dual-era and legacy-only servers (0 spawns per call), respawn in about 1.13 s, session-based upstream recovery, immediate list_changed to a running session, bearer plus Host and Origin, 70 s calls, progress, cancel, input_required on a modern HTTP upstream. No protocol translation, but it is custom code: this rig found 4 defects in it, and a hung upstream still costs 3 s per tools/list and hangs calls to that upstream.
- **agentgateway v1.7.0**: partial. Works through real Claude Code with a static bearer. Best operations: 42.8 MB, 125 ms cold start, hardening proven, only product relaying input_required. On a merged route: URIs rewritten and resource_link unreadable; every modern request spawns each dual-era stdio target (25 of 25, about 100 ms); one legacy-only target drops the backend to legacy with a child per session that is not respawned in that session and outlives the client; a running session never sees a new upstream; default 10 s upstream timeout needs a policy line; a hung stdio target stalls tools/list beyond 85 s.
- **1MCP v0.39.7**: partial. Works through real Claude Code. Best product stdio recovery (opt-in respawn), metadata kept, hot add reaches a running session in about 6 s, session-based upstream recovers. But URIs rewritten and resource_link unreadable; a legacy-only stdio server spawns per call (20 of 20) under a modern client; 318.8 MB RSS and 1.2 s cold start; no static bearer; 60 s call limit that requestTimeout did not change; no input_required relay; a hung upstream blocked a healthy one; a whole-endpoint outage for legacy clients when an HTTP upstream is down; pins SDK 1.30.0.
- **mcp-use 2.12.2 server.proxy()**: fail. Keeps outputSchema and annotations and relays progress and cancel, and stdio works through an undocumented connection path. But URIs rewritten, resource_link unreadable, _meta and instructions dropped, dead stdio child stays dead until restart, session-based upstream restart breaks it permanently, an upstream down at start is never retried, proxy() throws after listen(), bad Origin returns 200, 60 s call limit, no input_required relay, telemetry on by default. Not run through real Claude Code.
- **fastmcp-ts 1.9.0 mount()/createProxy() (npm @prefecthq/fastmcp-ts)**: fail. fetch(Request) works behind Hono and it holds one stable stdio child. But it drops outputSchema, annotations, _meta and instructions, rewrites URIs against its own documented invariant, relays neither progress nor cancel, crashes at start if an upstream is down, aborts on an unprefixed collision, and leaves a dead stdio child dead until restart. Not run through real Claude Code.

### Measurements

- **Environment**: AMD Ryzen 9 7900X3D, 24 threads, 30 GiB RAM, WSL2 kernel 6.18.54.1, Node v26.13.0, Claude Code 2.1.316 with claude-sonnet-5-5. No GPU work. (Load average about 2.5 to 6. All candidates ran on Node 26 except the agentgateway Rust binary. 13 real client runs cost about $0.39. Every npm install used --ignore-scripts and no package needed its scripts. Values are measured unless marked [docs] or [source].)
- **Versions and integrity**: agentgateway 1.7.0 sha256 1b2fc01a2de29ca113bbb6258b5cae7b1eb3c724071c09d687a449132f2f42f8, matching the .sha256 asset and the GitHub API digest. @modelcontextprotocol/server and client 2.4.0, hono adapter 2.0.2, node 2.1.2, hono 4.13.14, @hono/node-server 2.1.5, zod 4.6.7, @prefecthq/fastmcp-ts 1.9.0, mcp-use 2.12.2, @mcp-use/client 2.4.5, @1mcp/agent 0.39.7, inspector 2.13.0. (Install footprint: fastmcp-ts 149 packages and 50 MB, mcp-use 54 packages and 74 MB, 1MCP 202 packages and 110 MB, Inspector 108 MB.)
- **Stand-ins**: alpha: Streamable HTTP, tools status (outputSchema, structuredContent, annotations, _meta) and link_doc (resource_link), resource kb://alpha/snapshot/1. beta: stdio via serveStdio, dual-era, tools status (forces the collision) and beta_echo, resource beta://notes/1. (Added because the plain stand-ins were too easy: beta-legacy (2025 handshake only, server/discover returns -32601), ALPHA_STATEFUL=1 (legacy-only HTTP with real sessions), ALPHA_EXTRA=1 (slow tool, input_required tool, Korean URI). alpha and beta passed the probe directly in both eras as a control.)
- **Merged tool names**: agentgateway, fastmcp-ts, mcp-use, composition: alpha_status, alpha_link_doc, beta_status, beta_beta_echo. 1MCP: alpha_1mcp_status, alpha_1mcp_link_doc, beta_1mcp_status, beta_1mcp_beta_echo. (tools/list and tools/call to both upstreams passed on all five, legacy and modern. harness/probe.mjs, results/c*.json)
- **Collision handling**: All five prefix. An unprefixed fastmcp-ts mount aborts at start with Tool name collision on mount: "status". agentgateway prefixMode: conditional changed neither names nor URIs. (beta status against alpha status)
- **Tool metadata through each gateway**: structuredContent survived on all five. outputSchema and annotations: kept on agentgateway, mcp-use, 1MCP, composition; dropped on fastmcp-ts. title: kept on all five. _meta: kept on agentgateway and composition, kept by 1MCP with app.1mcp/route added; dropped on fastmcp-ts and mcp-use. (fastmcp-ts resyncTools copies only name, title, description and inputSchema [source])
- **Listed resource URIs**: agentgateway alpha+kb://alpha/snapshot/1. fastmcp-ts kb://alpha/alpha/snapshot/1. mcp-use mcp-use-proxy:///alpha/kb%3A%2F%2Falpha%2Fsnapshot%2F1. 1MCP mcp+1mcp.15070794f9a7cc24+kb://alpha/snapshot/1. Composition kb://alpha/snapshot/1, unchanged. (On resources/read, contents[].uri is rewritten by agentgateway and 1MCP and original on the other three. Each listed URI reads back in its own form.)
- **resource_link read-back**: Fails on all four maintained candidates, works on the composition. No candidate rewrites resource_link in tool results. agentgateway HTTP 500 -32603 legacy, HTTP 400 -32602 modern; fastmcp-ts -32602 Unknown resource; mcp-use -32602 Resource not found; 1MCP -32002 legacy, -32602 modern. (Raw URI from link_doc read through the same endpoint. No product has a setting for this: nothing in the agentgateway schema, and no resource URI option in 1MCP serve --help.)
- **Instructions, total characters**: Composition 99 ([name] headers only). agentgateway 240 (two-sentence preamble). 1MCP 1,732 (about 1,650 of boilerplate). fastmcp-ts none (no instructions option [source]). mcp-use none. (Upstream text totals 82 characters. Claude Code truncates at 4,096 [docs].)
- **Negotiated protocol revision**: Legacy client: 2025-11-25 on all five. 2026-07-28 client with dual-era upstreams: 2026-07-28 on all five. With a legacy-only target, agentgateway returns -32601 to server/discover for the whole backend, even with failOpen; the other four stay on 2026-07-28. (Raw probes, plus the official SDK client pinned with versionNegotiation mode pin 2026-07-28, which connected to all five. A legacy-only HTTP target triggered the same agentgateway behaviour.)
- **Stdio spawns, dual-era child, modern client**: agentgateway: every request, 8 of 8 and 25 of 25, including tools/call bound for alpha. fastmcp-ts, mcp-use, composition: 1 at start. 1MCP: 1 at start plus a discover probe. (Counted from beta's own spawn log, so short-lived children are not missed. harness/spawncount.sh, c1-agentgateway/matrix.sh)
- **Stdio spawns, legacy-only child, modern client**: 1MCP: every call, 20 of 20, p50 147 ms. agentgateway: backend drops to legacy with 1 child per client session. Composition: 0 per call over 20 calls, p50 2.5 ms. (harness/spawnrate.mjs, N=20. The same tool with a dual-era child on 1MCP: 0 spawns, p50 24.4 ms.)
- **agentgateway session and child lifetime**: 5 concurrent legacy sessions made 5 children, about 508 MB for the tree. DELETE reaps the child. A child outlives Claude Code, which sent no DELETE. With sessionTtl 6s the child went between 25 and 30 s, and the session then returned 404. (Default TTL is 30 minutes [docs]. After TTL, reuse returned session not found with HTTP 404.)
- **Stateless HTTP upstream down and back**: agentgateway failOpen and composition: its tools leave the list, others keep working. fastmcp-ts and mcp-use: stale list, calls return isError fetch failed. 1MCP modern: tools leave the list, others fine. All five recover without restart on return. (harness/lifecycle.mjs)
- **1MCP legacy-session outage**: One HTTP upstream down took the whole endpoint down for legacy clients: 8 of 8 samples failed over 24 s with beta healthy, 404 on existing sessions and 500 on new ones. Also failed with --enable-async-loading --async-background-retry. Modern clients degraded cleanly to 2 tools. (harness/outage.mjs. Claude Code is not exposed, because it stays on the modern path against 1MCP.)
- **Session-based HTTP upstream restart**: 1MCP recovers in about 2 s. agentgateway: that session stays broken and a new session works. fastmcp-ts and mcp-use: broken until gateway restart, even for new sessions. Composition: failed on first version, now recovers on the first retry. (ALPHA_STATEFUL=1, harness/stateful.sh, logs/stateful.txt. The first-version failure was fixed by a retry on SdkHttpError status 404.)
- **Stdio child SIGKILL**: agentgateway: dead for that legacy session and its tools leave the list, a new session respawns; on the modern path the next request spawns anyway. fastmcp-ts and mcp-use: Not connected until gateway restart, with tools still listed, and new sessions fail too. 1MCP and composition: respawned. (harness/lifecycle.mjs. 1MCP respawn is opt-in, used restartOnExit true, maxRestarts 5, restartDelay 200.)
- **Time to first good call after child SIGKILL**: 1MCP 476, 725, 1070, 1862, 3499 ms, exponential backoff. Composition 1124 to 1140 ms, 5 of 5, fixed interval. (harness/respawn.mjs, 5 consecutive kills on the modern path. The composition has no crash-loop limit yet.)
- **Upstream down at gateway start**: agentgateway unaffected, no connection at boot. fastmcp-ts process crashes (unhandled fetch failed). mcp-use skips the upstream and never retries it. 1MCP starts in about 1.3 s, not recovered at +2.5 s in default mode. Composition retries and the upstream appears unaided. (alpha stopped before gateway start. The 1MCP async retry mode was not tested for this case.)
- **Gateway SIGKILL**: Stdio child exited within 0.8 s on all candidates with a persistent child. On agentgateway the sample had no live child at the time. (The child exits because SDK servers stop on stdin EOF. A server ignoring EOF was not tested.)

### Surprises

- Harness conflict: the task required report.md, but Write was refused with 'Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files'. I did not bypass it through Bash. No report file exists.
- All four maintained candidates fail resource_link read-back, each with a different URI scheme. VG-C10 predicted this for agentgateway only, and it also rewrites contents[].uri on read. prefixMode: conditional does not help.
- VG-C4 is worse than stated: on the modern path agentgateway spawns every stdio target on every request, even a tools/call bound for another target (25 of 25). The alpha reply does not wait for it, so alpha p50 stayed at 7.2 ms.
- VG-C6 is narrower than stated: only a legacy-only target drops the backend to legacy. A dual-era stdio target answers server/discover and the route stays modern, despite the README wording. failOpen does not help the legacy-only case.
- 1MCP's cross-era handling has a hidden cost: a legacy-only stdio upstream under a modern client spawns per call (20 of 20), while a dual-era one spawns 0.
- One HTTP upstream down takes 1MCP's whole endpoint offline for legacy clients (8 of 8 samples over 24 s), but not for modern ones, so Claude Code is not exposed.
- Only 1MCP recovered unaided from a session-based upstream restart on the same session. My first composition failed that test outright.
- fastmcp-ts contradicts its own docs: the documented URI invariant is false at 1.9.0, because prefixResourceUri inserts the prefix. npm fastmcp-ts is an unrelated package (0.1.2, another author); the real name is @prefecthq/fastmcp-ts.
- mcp-use docs say HTTP upstreams only, but proxy() accepts any duck-typed connection, and a stdio @mcp-use/client connection worked. Its telemetry is on by default, which no research report mentioned.
- agentgateway fails any MCP call over 10 s by default (upstream call timeout). This affects real tools and needs a route policy.
- 1MCP's requestTimeout had no effect on a 70 s call. It was the only setting that looked applicable.
- A running Claude Code session keeps subscriptions/listen open and refreshes on list_changed. That makes hot add a real differentiator: agentgateway sends none, so it never updates a running session.
- Tool-level anthropic/alwaysLoad survives agentgateway, 1MCP and the composition, and Claude Code honours it. This softens brief item X2.
- SDK trap for the KB, with no gateway involved: McpServer lists a static non-ASCII URI raw but looks it up via new URL(uri).href, which percent-encodes it, so kb://alpha/스냅샷/1 lists and then returns Resource not found. A template works; percent-encode or use templates.
- The SDK's LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 2025-11-25 and its client defaults to legacy. A 2026-07-28 client needs versionNegotiation set explicitly.
- No candidate fully handles a hung upstream. Cached lists (fastmcp-ts, mcp-use) did best here, which is why a last-good list is on the composition's to-do list.
- Mistakes in my own work, all corrected and rechecked: a shell bug made standalone stop a no-op (logs show instances never overlapped, so the matrix stands); a ~1 s cold-start outlier on every candidate was a dropped SYN in my polling, so the tables use a bounded re-run; the Korean URI first looked like a gateway failure until a direct control showed the SDK behaviour; a 1MCP hot-add 'failure' was a race in my test; my tap initially hid long-lived streams.
- Side effect, corrected: --no-session-persistence stops transcripts, but claude -p still created an empty ~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/memory/ per run. I removed all of mine with rmdir (12 directories, plus one after the final run). An s2-lifecycle-cc-cwd entry from another spike remains and was left alone; other spikes will leave the same.

## Spike 2

Recommendation: socket-activated, started on first connection, then long-running, with no idle exit in v1. listen({fd:3}) works via createAdaptorServer. Cold start p50/p95: 164/204 ms for /healthz, 187/214 ms for MCP tools/call (N=30). Idle RSS is about 93 MB. Real Claude Code 2.1.316 connected in 238 ms with only the socket up, and survived SIGKILL between calls with no tool error. A plain server that was down cost a 30 s stall per attempt and lost the tools. Five restarts under load: 0 failures with the socket held, 289 with a plain port. Key finding: Claude Code holds subscriptions/listen open for the whole session when listChanged is declared, so idle exit either never fires or flaps. Fresh connections never failed across idle exits; all tagged failures were on reused keep-alive sockets. A sync 200 ms handler stalls MCP and SSE fully, and a worker removes that. On 127.0.0.1 here, a closed port hangs instead of refusing. Default start limits can kill the socket. The report .md was NOT written: the harness refused it, so this result is the report. Not tested: interactive Claude Code, the 10-13 min retry, closing the last session, WSL stop, node:sqlite in a worker, a real aggregator. All 14 real-client runs were N=1, `-p` mode, haiku, about $0.01 total. Host: WSL2 mirrored networking, 24 CPUs, Node 26.13.0, systemd 259. No GPU involved; other spikes shared the host.

### Recommendation

Use socket activation with no idle exit in v1. The process starts on the first connection and stays up. The port is a placeholder because X14 is open. Equivalent settings were tested via transient units; these exact files, Requires=, [Install] and %C were not run.

sagae-control.socket:
[Socket] ListenStream=127.0.0.1:8787, NoDelay=true. [Install] WantedBy=sockets.target.

sagae-control.service (no [Install]):
[Unit] Requires=sagae-control.socket, After=sagae-control.socket, StartLimitIntervalSec=0.
[Service] Type=simple, WorkingDirectory=<absolute path>, ExecStart=/home/user/.nvm/versions/node/v26.13.0/bin/node dist/server.mjs, Environment=NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=%C/sagae-control/compile-cache, Restart=always, RestartSec=1, TimeoutStopSec=8.

App rules:
1. Use createAdaptorServer plus server.listen({fd:3}) when LISTEN_FDS and LISTEN_PID match. Delete those variables afterwards. Fall back to 127.0.0.1:PORT for local runs.
2. On SIGTERM: server.close(), closeIdleConnections(), then closeAllConnections() after 1-2 s. Otherwise a Claude Code listen stream holds the stop until the timeout.
3. Keep declaring tools.listChanged. Adding upstreams without changing Claude Code config depends on it, and it is what makes Claude Code open the session-long stream.
4. Never run synchronous queries on the main thread. Use a worker or a separate process.
5. Keep work before listen() small. Start stdio upstreams after listening or lazily, because missing the 5 s discover probe pins the session to legacy.
6. ExecStart must exec Node directly, so LISTEN_PID matches (read from docs).

Install, for the user: systemctl --user enable --now sagae-control.socket, plus loginctl enable-linger sagae. Linger is required for L1. For L0 it removes the remaining dependency on a login session. Neither was run here. An nvm upgrade changes the absolute ExecStart path.

If idle exit is wanted later, all of these apply: Restart=on-failure instead of always (not measured); a StartLimitIntervalSec that normal activations cannot hit; count every open stream as activity; timeout above keepAliveTimeout + buffer (6 s), in practice at least 10 minutes.

### Verdicts

- **Plain long-running process that binds the port itself**: fail. Down at Claude Code startup means a 30 s stall per attempt and tool loss (R3a, R3e). About 58 refused requests per restart. 2 of 3 tool calls failed when stopped mid-session (R4)
- **Socket-activated with idle exit, open streams counted**: partial. Safe, with 0 failures for fresh connections and when keep-alive is shorter than idle. But subscriptions/listen is open for the whole Claude Code session, so it does not exit during any open session. Savings are about 94 MB plus about 78 MB per stdio child
- **Socket-activated with idle exit, listen stream not counted**: fail. Tool calls still work, but the process flaps (4 activations in 12 s) and the client gives up on re-listen after 3 drops, losing tool-list notifications for the session (R2d)
- **Socket-activated, started on demand, no idle exit, Restart=always**: pass. Startup connected with the app stopped (R1), SIGKILL between calls caused no tool error (R8), 0 of 6,665 failed across restarts, crash loop kept the socket and recovered (7.76 s). Exact unit files were not installed; equivalent settings were tested through transient units
- **Default systemd limits with socket activation**: fail. 6th quick activation or a crash loop ends in service-start-limit-hit, the socket unit fails and releases the port (measured). Needs StartLimitIntervalSec=0
- **Synchronous node:sqlite on the main thread**: fail. Stalls every MCP call and SSE stream for the full query. Queued queries reach about 1.6 s. A worker thread removes the effect (measured with a spin loop in the worker, not sqlite)

### Surprises

- Claude Code 2.1.316 opens subscriptions/listen right after discover and holds it for the whole session when the server declares tools.listChanged. The SDK declares it by default. This decides the idle-exit question and answers the open item in http-gateway.md about whether Claude Code opens such a stream.
- When the listen stream drops, the client re-listens at about 1, 2 and 4 s, and each re-listen reactivates the app. After 3 quick drops it gives up for that session. Tool calls keep working, but notifications do not.
- On this mirrored WSL host, a closed 127.0.0.1 port hangs instead of refusing, starting 50-400 ms after close. A raw connect ran 133 s. 127.0.0.2, ::1 and <LAN-IP> refuse instantly. So a plain server that is down costs 30 s per attempt here, not a fast failure.
- VG-C19 needs refining for 2.1.316 in -p mode. Startup failures get 3 more attempts, covering about 6 s with instant refusal and about 126 s with the hang. A server appearing inside that window is picked up. After the window it was not.
- A late connection falls to the legacy protocol because the 5 s version probe timed out (R3c, R3d). That session has no listen stream, so a slow start has a lasting cost.
- Default systemd limits are dangerous: 5 quick activations or a crash loop fail the socket unit and release the port, which is worse than a plain server failing.
- Fresh connections never failed across idle exits, even with process.exit, because systemd holds the listener. Every tagged failure was on a reused keep-alive socket, and the same failure occurs with no idle exit at all.
- Node 26 adds keepAliveTimeoutBuffer (default 1000 ms) to keepAliveTimeout, so lowering keepAliveTimeout alone did not remove the race (36 of 1,168 failed).
- A CONN_CLOSE test variant was discarded: curl showed connection: close, but clients still failed on reused sockets, and I did not find out why.
- The Write tool refused the required report.md as a subagent report file, so no report exists at the given path. This result carries the findings instead.
- Harness slips, corrected: zsh globbing broke the first active-SSE run, so it was rerun. Claude Code's Bash tool blocked a standalone sleep 45 in R3d, so the model used a background command, and later runs used a wait script.

### Surprises

- The report file could not be written: the harness blocks subagent report files, so report.md is absent despite the task asking for it.
- Orval's default fetch client resolves a 404 as success in TanStack Query: isError stays false and the Problem arrives as data, while the hook declares TError=ProblemResponse. Types alone never show this.
- A renamed as_of axis passed in a stored object produced zero tsc errors, because excess-property checks apply only to fresh literals. For a time-travel viewer this would show current data as if historical. Fixed with satisfies plus unknown-parameter rejection in the mock.
- Removing a field from required is not caught by tsc at all, so contract review cannot rely on types alone.
- The brief's named 3.1 features did not separate the candidates at all; differences appeared only under the stress spec and at runtime.
- The audit picture is inverted from the research: js-yaml is clean on openapi-typescript but exact-pinned vulnerable on Hey API, the proposed replacement. openapi-typescript's remaining findings come from minimatch.
- @kubb/plugin-client emits imports of ../.kubb/client but never writes that file; @kubb/plugin-fetch is the one that does. Kubb v5 plugins also version independently of kubb itself (5.15.3 with plugin-ts 5.4.0, plugin-fetch 5.11.0).
- Kubb's full generation takes 11.5 s against about 0.57 s for the others, and 1.5 s for its own types-only mode. Cause not investigated.
- ajv's discriminator:true cannot be used with OpenAPI mapping at all, and ajv strict mode caught a real YAML bug in my contract that all four generators accepted silently.
- Opaque cursors surface as a Schemathesis ST202 failure: a schema-valid cursor cannot be honoured, so the real contract must state the 400 rule explicitly.
- Schemathesis --seed does not fix stateful case counts: seed 4 gave 1,435 then 845 cases, all phases complete. Do not assert exact counts in CI.
- Orval output depends on the project's tsconfig and package.json (.ts extensions, an Awaited shim), so a TS 7 comparison without them shows a false difference.
- Several results had to be corrected as my own harness bugs, not tool defects: a misplaced ts-expect-error, a suite regex that matched the wrong file, greedy sed, zsh not word-splitting, and yaml@2.8.1 that I chose myself (audit moderate, bumped to 2.9.1). Reported numbers are from the final clean run.
- The pkill pattern killed my own shell once; the mock was restarted and tracked by PID from then on. Listeners on 18090, 18101, 18102, 18150 and 18310 belonged to other processes and were not touched.

## Adversarial review

Core spike conclusions hold, but S1's "passes every check" does not. Reruns reproduced agentgateway spawns (25/25), 1MCP per-call spawns, S2 fd:3 and the start-limit trap, S3 real-GPU 165 fps including the never-run recommended combination, FA2, and the S4 end-to-end flow. The composition also worked with real Python and TS SDK 1.30 stdio servers (one child, 2-4 ms). That strengthens its lead: a real Python server is silently invisible through agentgateway failOpen on Claude Code's default path, and 1MCP spawns per call (355 ms). New composition defects: a config typo kills the gateway, duplicate URIs return the wrong upstream's body, the first tools/list is partial (20/20, hidden by S1's polling), and edits to an existing upstream are ignored. S1's upstream-down tests ran inside TIME_WAIT; after about 60 s connects hang on this host. The composition is a custom gateway: about 300 lines by estimate plus 1,420 harness lines, and "no translation" holds only at wire level. A maintained route now has evidence: agentgateway plus mcp-proxy worked through real Claude Code with one stable child, but it stays legacy, has no live hot add, and a dead child is never respawned. One registration holds for connection; unattended use needs a blanket or per-upstream allow rule, and wildcards work. Decision needed: accept the custom gateway, or the adapter chain. No report file was written. Only small residue remains.

## Spike 5

KB 계약의 규모 추정(개요 기본 프로필 노드 2만~5만, 엣지 5만~20만)으로 S3를 다시 쟀다. 레이아웃과 페이로드는 두 규모 모두 쟀고 렌더는 일부만 유효하다. KB 데이터 파일이 없어 그래프는 합성이다. 자체 worker의 FA2 300회는 20k/80k 18.9 s, 50k/200k 57.1 s로 Node보다 8~9% 느렸고 메인 스레드 rAF는 p50 6.06 ms였다. 페이로드는 50k/200k도 컬럼 JSON 19 MB, 파싱 75 ms 이하로 병목이 아니다. 렌더는 Orca 탭의 표시 주기가 깨져 fps, rAF, 20 ms 초과 프레임이 무효다(2026-11-01 정정: 원인은 GPU 경합이 아니라 호스트였다. 이 절 끝의 "2026-11-01 재측정" 참조). 읽을 수 있는 값에서 20k/80k는 첫 프레임과 CPU+GPU 예산을 넘었고 50k/200k는 오버레이를 뺀 항목을 넘었다. heap은 gc 값이 없는 상한이다. 이 절은 적대적 리뷰를 거치지 않았고 윗절의 리뷰 규칙이 적용되지 않는다. 재현 자산은 `docs/research/spikes/s5-scale/`에 있다.

### Recommendation

레이아웃은 브라우저 자체 worker의 `assign`을 유지한다. Node 대비 비용이 8~9%이고 메인 스레드를 흔들지 않는다. 기본 개요는 노드 1만, 엣지 5만 이하로 둔다. 계약 기본 `limit`, `edge_limit`과 같다. KB의 기본 타입 질문은 이 크기를 넘지 않는 필터로 답한다. 2만 보기는 사용자가 고르는 동작으로 두고 경고한다. 첫 프레임이 약 1 s다. 50k/200k는 전체 그래프로 그리지 않는다. 막는 것은 페이로드가 아니라 렌더와 heap이다.

측정 보고는 2만 초과에 Node `loupe layout`을 권했다. 근거는 `(build_id, scope)` 키와 "5분마다 빌드"였다. 계약 대조에서 그 전제가 틀렸다. 5분은 게시 간격이고 봉투의 `build_id`는 그때 바뀌지 않는다. `loupe.md` 6.2절은 키를 위상 해시로 바꾸고 소프트 미스를 넣은 뒤 Node를 출구 조건으로 옮겼다.

GPU가 조용할 때 `run-all.sh`로 렌더 행을 다시 재서 fps와 20 ms 초과 프레임을 얻는다. gc를 켠 heap을 함께 잰다. 15k/60k 천장은 외삽이고 재지 않았다.

### Verdicts

- **브라우저 자체 worker의 `assign`, 20k/80k와 50k/200k**: pass. Node 대비 8~9%, rAF p50 6.06 ms. 실행마다 한 번의 끊김은 원인 미확인이다
- **Node `assign`, 20k/80k와 50k/200k**: pass. 17.5 s, 52.4 s. 300회로 수렴한다
- **브라우저의 컬럼 JSON 파싱과 gunzip**: pass. 50k/200k도 파싱 75 ms 이하, gunzip 88 ms 이하다
- **렌더 10.5k/26.9k**: partial. 첫 프레임, 오버레이, 호버, heap 상한은 예산 안이다. CPU+GPU p95가 3회 중 1회 10.1 ms다. 엣지가 S3의 약 절반이다
- **렌더 20k/80k**: fail. 첫 프레임 924~1,244 ms, CPU+GPU p95 8.3~12.0 ms. GPU 경합이 값을 부풀렸을 수 있어 확정은 아니다(2026-11-01 정정: 경합이 아니었다. 같은 20k/80k의 Chrome 창 값은 아래 재측정에 있다)
- **렌더 50k/200k**: fail. 첫 프레임 2.4~2.7 s, CPU+GPU p95 19~24 ms, 호버 p95 63~67 ms
- **fps, rAF, 20 ms 초과 프레임**: not_tested. 무효다
- **브라우저 zstd 해제**: not_tested. `DecompressionStream`에 zstd가 없다
- **패키지 `FA2Layout` worker, 클릭 dim-all, 방향·다중 엣지**: not_tested

### Surprises

- 렌더가 끝까지 정상 주기로 돌지 못했다. 표시 주기가 vsync의 14배와 165배로 묶인 것은 WebGL 탭에서만 나타났고 null rAF에는 없었다.
- 50k 레이아웃의 메인 스레드 끊김이 3회 모두 약 9.3 s에 279, 364, 345 ms로 났다. 원인을 찾지 못했다.
- 이전 20k 호버 실행 1회가 `Sigma: edge "40815" can't be repaint`를 던졌다. 뒤의 6개 셀에서 재발하지 않았다. 원인 미상, N=1이다(`out/log-s5.jsonl`).
- `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory`가 Orca에서 막혀 있어 heap은 상한만 얻었다. S3의 63 MB는 gc를 켠 값이라 직접 비교할 수 없다.
- 첫 프레임과 CPU+GPU가 노드 + 엣지에 거의 선형이다. 15k/60k 천장은 여기서 나온 외삽이다.
- `tab create`를 그냥 쓰면 탭이 다른 worktree에 열렸다. `--worktree path:/home/user/sagae-tools`로 바꿨다. `tab close --page`가 worktree 없이 7개 탭에서 조용히 실패해 `--worktree id:`로 모두 닫았다.
- `pkill -f` 한 번이 자기 셸을 죽였다(exit 144). 다른 영향은 없었다.

**시간 초과 (300 s, 결과 줄 없음).** RTX 창의 50k rep 1과 Radeon의 sub10k rep 0이다. 두 셀은 값이 없다. 그래서 50k는 RTX에서 1회뿐이다. Radeon sub10k는 rep 1 한 번뿐이다. 시험 중 GPU 사용률 표본은 1~6%였다(`nv-all.log`, `radeon-all.log`).

**발견 1: Orca 탭이 문제였고 GPU 경합이 아니었다.** 같은 머신, 같은 어댑터(RTX 4080 SUPER)에서 Orca 탭은 gltest p50 60.6 ms(WebGL 어댑터 시험의 low-power, high-performance, default는 48.5, 42.4, 60.6 ms), Chrome 창은 6.06 ms다. Orca 탭의 이 실행 중 GPU 사용률은 5개 표본이 30, 1, 15, 3, 2%(중앙값 3%)로 GPU는 놀고 있었다. 이전 S5 본문이 60~85 ms를 "GPU 경합"으로 읽은 것은 틀렸다. 앞선 `nvidia-smi` 36~40%와 다른 Chrome 프로세스 34%가 원인이라는 증거는 이번 실행에서 나오지 않았다. 원인이 Orca 탭의 어떤 상태(포커스 없음, Chrome 150, 임베드)인지는 가르지 못했다. No maintained candidate is acceptable as shipped. agentgateway, 1MCP, mcp-use and fastmcp-ts all rewrite resource URIs but not resource_link, so a link in a tool result cannot be read back (reproduced through real Claude Code on agentgateway and 1MCP). The least custom code with acceptable fidelity is the SDK composition. It respects the no-translation rule: none of its lines parse JSON-RPC or handle eras, Mcp-Name or session headers, because the SDK does that on both legs. What the project owns is routing and lifecycle. That ownership has a real cost: this rig found 4 defects in my first version (no recovery from a restarted session-based upstream, the 60 s SDK default cutting long calls, no input_required relay, one hung upstream stalling tools/list for 60 s), and fixing them took 30 lines. - fastmcp-ts contradicts its own docs: the documented URI invariant is false at 1.9.0, because prefixResourceUri inserts the prefix. npm fastmcp-ts is an unrelated package (0.1.2, another author); the real name is @prefecthq/fastmcp-ts.
- mcp-use docs say HTTP upstreams only, but proxy() accepts any duck-typed connection, and a stdio @mcp-use/client connection worked. Its telemetry is on by default, which no research report mentioned.
- agentgateway fails any MCP call over 10 s by default (upstream call timeout). This affects real tools and needs a route policy.
- 1MCP's requestTimeout had no effect on a 70 s call. It was the only setting that looked applicable.
- A running Claude Code session keeps subscriptions/listen open and refreshes on list_changed. That makes hot add a real differentiator: agentgateway sends none, so it never updates a running session.
- Tool-level anthropic/alwaysLoad survives agentgateway, 1MCP and the composition, and Claude Code honours it. This softens brief item X2.
- SDK trap for the KB, with no gateway involved: McpServer lists a static non-ASCII URI raw but looks it up via new URL(uri).href, which percent-encodes it, so kb://alpha/스냅샷/1 lists and then returns Resource not found. A template works; percent-encode or use templates.
- The SDK's LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 2025-11-25 and its client defaults to legacy. A 2026-07-28 client needs versionNegotiation set explicitly.
- No candidate fully handles a hung upstream. Cached lists (fastmcp-ts, mcp-use) did best here, which is why a last-good list is on the composition's to-do list.
- Mistakes in my own work, all corrected and rechecked: a shell bug made standalone stop a no-op (logs show instances never overlapped, so the matrix stands); a ~1 s cold-start outlier on every candidate was a dropped SYN in my polling, so the tables use a bounded re-run; the Korean URI first looked like a gateway failure until a direct control showed the SDK behaviour; a 1MCP hot-add 'failure' was a race in my test; my tap initially hid long-lived streams.
- Side effect, corrected: --no-session-persistence stops transcripts, but claude -p still created an empty ~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/memory/ per run. I removed all of mine with rmdir (12 directories, plus one after the final run). An s2-lifecycle-cc-cwd entry from another spike remains and was left alone; other spikes will leave the same.

## Spike 2

Recommendation: socket-activated, started on first connection, then long-running, with no idle exit in v1. listen({fd:3}) works via createAdaptorServer. Cold start p50/p95: 164/204 ms for /healthz, 187/214 ms for MCP tools/call (N=30). Idle RSS is about 93 MB. Real Claude Code 2.1.316 connected in 238 ms with only the socket up, and survived SIGKILL between calls with no tool error. A plain server that was down cost a 30 s stall per attempt and lost the tools. Five restarts under load: 0 failures with the socket held, 289 with a plain port. Key finding: Claude Code holds subscriptions/listen open for the whole session when listChanged is declared, so idle exit either never fires or flaps. Fresh connections never failed across idle exits; all tagged failures were on reused keep-alive sockets. A sync 200 ms handler stalls MCP and SSE fully, and a worker removes that. On 127.0.0.1 here, a closed port hangs instead of refusing. Default start limits can kill the socket. The report .md was NOT written: the harness refused it, so this result is the report. Not tested: interactive Claude Code, the 10-13 min retry, closing the last session, WSL stop, node:sqlite in a worker, a real aggregator. All 14 real-client runs were N=1, `-p` mode, haiku, about $0.01 total. Host: WSL2 mirrored networking, 24 CPUs, Node 26.13.0, systemd 259. No GPU involved; other spikes shared the host.

### Recommendation

Use socket activation with no idle exit in v1. The process starts on the first connection and stays up. The port is a placeholder because X14 is open. Equivalent settings were tested via transient units; these exact files, Requires=, [Install] and %C were not run.

sagae-control.socket:
[Socket] ListenStream=127.0.0.1:8787, NoDelay=true. [Install] WantedBy=sockets.target.

sagae-control.service (no [Install]):
[Unit] Requires=sagae-control.socket, After=sagae-control.socket, StartLimitIntervalSec=0.
[Service] Type=simple, WorkingDirectory=<absolute path>, ExecStart=/home/user/.nvm/versions/node/v26.13.0/bin/node dist/server.mjs, Environment=NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=%C/sagae-control/compile-cache, Restart=always, RestartSec=1, TimeoutStopSec=8.

App rules:
1. Use createAdaptorServer plus server.listen({fd:3}) when LISTEN_FDS and LISTEN_PID match. Delete those variables afterwards. Fall back to 127.0.0.1:PORT for local runs.
2. On SIGTERM: server.close(), closeIdleConnections(), then closeAllConnections() after 1-2 s. Otherwise a Claude Code listen stream holds the stop until the timeout.
3. Keep declaring tools.listChanged. Adding upstreams without changing Claude Code config depends on it, and it is what makes Claude Code open the session-long stream.
4. Never run synchronous queries on the main thread. Use a worker or a separate process.
5. Keep work before listen() small. Start stdio upstreams after listening or lazily, because missing the 5 s discover probe pins the session to legacy.
6. ExecStart must exec Node directly, so LISTEN_PID matches (read from docs).

Install, for the user: systemctl --user enable --now sagae-control.socket, plus loginctl enable-linger sagae. Linger is required for L1. For L0 it removes the remaining dependency on a login session. Neither was run here. An nvm upgrade changes the absolute ExecStart path.

If idle exit is wanted later, all of these apply: Restart=on-failure instead of always (not measured); a StartLimitIntervalSec that normal activations cannot hit; count every open stream as activity; timeout above keepAliveTimeout + buffer (6 s), in practice at least 10 minutes.

### Verdicts

- **Plain long-running process that binds the port itself**: fail. Down at Claude Code startup means a 30 s stall per attempt and tool loss (R3a, R3e). About 58 refused requests per restart. 2 of 3 tool calls failed when stopped mid-session (R4)
- **Socket-activated with idle exit, open streams counted**: partial. Safe, with 0 failures for fresh connections and when keep-alive is shorter than idle. But subscriptions/listen is open for the whole Claude Code session, so it does not exit during any open session. Savings are about 94 MB plus about 78 MB per stdio child
- **Socket-activated with idle exit, listen stream not counted**: fail. Tool calls still work, but the process flaps (4 activations in 12 s) and the client gives up on re-listen after 3 drops, losing tool-list notifications for the session (R2d)
- **Socket-activated, started on demand, no idle exit, Restart=always**: pass. Startup connected with the app stopped (R1), SIGKILL between calls caused no tool error (R8), 0 of 6,665 failed across restarts, crash loop kept the socket and recovered (7.76 s). Exact unit files were not installed; equivalent settings were tested through transient units
- **Default systemd limits with socket activation**: fail. 6th quick activation or a crash loop ends in service-start-limit-hit, the socket unit fails and releases the port (measured). Needs StartLimitIntervalSec=0
- **Synchronous node:sqlite on the main thread**: fail. Stalls every MCP call and SSE stream for the full query. Queued queries reach about 1.6 s. A worker thread removes the effect (measured with a spin loop in the worker, not sqlite)

### Surprises

- Claude Code 2.1.316 opens subscriptions/listen right after discover and holds it for the whole session when the server declares tools.listChanged. The SDK declares it by default. This decides the idle-exit question and answers the open item in http-gateway.md about whether Claude Code opens such a stream.
- When the listen stream drops, the client re-listens at about 1, 2 and 4 s, and each re-listen reactivates the app. After 3 quick drops it gives up for that session. Tool calls keep working, but notifications do not.
- On this mirrored WSL host, a closed 127.0.0.1 port hangs instead of refusing, starting 50-400 ms after close. A raw connect ran 133 s. 127.0.0.2, ::1 and <LAN-IP> refuse instantly. So a plain server that is down costs 30 s per attempt here, not a fast failure.
- VG-C19 needs refining for 2.1.316 in -p mode. Startup failures get 3 more attempts, covering about 6 s with instant refusal and about 126 s with the hang. A server appearing inside that window is picked up. After the window it was not.
- A late connection falls to the legacy protocol because the 5 s version probe timed out (R3c, R3d). That session has no listen stream, so a slow start has a lasting cost.
- Default systemd limits are dangerous: 5 quick activations or a crash loop fail the socket unit and release the port, which is worse than a plain server failing.
- Fresh connections never failed across idle exits, even with process.exit, because systemd holds the listener. Every tagged failure was on a reused keep-alive socket, and the same failure occurs with no idle exit at all.
- Node 26 adds keepAliveTimeoutBuffer (default 1000 ms) to keepAliveTimeout, so lowering keepAliveTimeout alone did not remove the race (36 of 1,168 failed).
- A CONN_CLOSE test variant was discarded: curl showed connection: close, but clients still failed on reused sockets, and I did not find out why.
- The Write tool refused the required report.md as a subagent report file, so no report exists at the given path. This result carries the findings instead.
- Harness slips, corrected: zsh globbing broke the first active-SSE run, so it was rerun. Claude Code's Bash tool blocked a standalone sleep 45 in R3d, so the model used a background command, and later runs used a wait script.

## Adversarial review

Core spike conclusions hold, but S1's "passes every check" does not. Reruns reproduced agentgateway spawns (25/25), 1MCP per-call spawns, S2 fd:3 and the start-limit trap, S3 real-GPU 165 fps including the never-run recommended combination, FA2, and the S4 end-to-end flow. The composition also worked with real Python and TS SDK 1.30 stdio servers (one child, 2-4 ms). That strengthens its lead: a real Python server is silently invisible through agentgateway failOpen on Claude Code's default path, and 1MCP spawns per call (355 ms). New composition defects: a config typo kills the gateway, duplicate URIs return the wrong upstream's body, the first tools/list is partial (20/20, hidden by S1's polling), and edits to an existing upstream are ignored. S1's upstream-down tests ran inside TIME_WAIT; after about 60 s connects hang on this host. The composition is a custom gateway: about 300 lines by estimate plus 1,420 harness lines, and "no translation" holds only at wire level. A maintained route now has evidence: agentgateway plus mcp-proxy worked through real Claude Code with one stable child, but it stays legacy, has no live hot add, and a dead child is never respawned. One registration holds for connection; unattended use needs a blanket or per-upstream allow rule, and wildcards work. Decision needed: accept the custom gateway, or the adapter chain. No report file was written. Only small residue remains.

- **contradicted** [S1] The composition is the only candidate to pass every check, and resource_link read-back works on it.
  - Evidence: Unmodified gateway.mjs with two HTTP stand-ins that both expose kb://alpha/snapshot/1: one_link_doc returned the link, and resources/read of that URI returned serverInfo 'two' (N=1). uriOwner is one global map and the last lister wins. S1's stand-ins had disjoint URIs, so this path never ran. S1's own table also shows calls to a hung upstream running past 85 s.
  - Correction: Read-back works only for disjoint URIs. A collision silently returns the wrong upstream's body. The design needs a duplicate-URI rule. S1's to-do names one, but its verdict presents read-back as solved.
- **contradicted** [S1] Hot add by file watch needs no restart, and the full regression passed on the final revision.
  - Evidence: A truncated JSON write killed the gateway within 0.5 s (uncaught SyntaxError in the reload timer), and the listener and stdio children went with it. An upstream name containing an underscore did the same (N=1 each). Under S2's Restart=always, RestartSec=1, StartLimitIntervalSec=0 in a transient unit: the socket stayed active, the service looped, curl hit its 5 s limit (exit 28), and service was back within 2.5 s of the fix (N=1). Changing an existing upstream's URL was silently ignored (N=1).
  - Correction: Adding a server is this tool's core operation, and one typo currently takes every MCP server down. Keep the last good config in a try/catch and detect changed entries. About 10 lines by estimate.
- **contradicted** [S1] A legacy-only target makes agentgateway return -32601 for the whole backend, and failOpen is a safe hardening line for the merged route and the strict-rule fallback.
  - Evidence: That holds for -32601 servers only. A real Python SDK mcp 1.30.0 FastMCP server answers server/discover with -32602 and stays alive. A real TS SDK 1.30.0 server gives -32601. agentgateway failOpen with the Python stdio target on the modern path returned only alpha tools. Real Claude Code showed status connected, 2 init tools, and could not find the Python tool (N=1, 5 spawns). Default failureMode passed -32602 through, Claude Code fell back to legacy, and all 4 tools worked (N=1, 2 spawns).
  - Correction: failOpen with a Python legacy stdio target is a silent tool loss on Claude Code's default path. Do not list failOpen as a safe setting for stdio targets.
- **contradicted** [S1] With an upstream down, composition and agentgateway failOpen drop its tools and others keep working (4.6 ms). agentgateway is unaffected and 1MCP starts in about 1.3 s with an upstream down at start.
  - Evidence: S1 sampled about 200 ms after stopping alpha. At +12 to +15 s a stopped upstream still failed fast (composition 6 ms, agentgateway 3.8 ms). At +75 s, with TIME_WAIT sockets on the port gone from 2 to 0: composition tools/list 3,004 ms twice, call to the down upstream 10,427 ms then -32603; agentgateway failOpen server/discover 10,030 ms, tools/list 997 and 10,003 ms. Never-bound target, real Claude Code on agentgateway failOpen: connect 21,017 ms, probe timed out, pinned legacy, init status pending, wall 36.6 s (N=1). 1MCP with a never-bound upstream opened its port after about 17 s (N=1). The composition is unaffected only when the upstream never connected (5-10 ms). TIME_WAIT as the cause is inference from these observations.
  - Correction: Long-down loopback upstreams hang on this host. Composition pays 3 s per list; agentgateway pays 10 s per request and pins sessions to legacy. An untried setting helps: config.backend.connectTimeout 1s gave discover 1,031 ms, lists about 1,004 ms, and real Claude Code connected in 2,020 ms with no legacy pin (N=1). Every design needs short connect timeouts.
- **contradicted** [S2] A closed 127.0.0.1 port gives ECONNREFUSED for 50-400 ms after close, then hangs.
  - Evidence: The window is not a fixed number. S2's porttest reproduced (hang from 51 and 509 ms). Separate process killed with SIGKILL: refused at +100 ms, hang from +1 s to +30 s. In-process close with one probe per port: refused up to +5 s, hang from +10 s to +180 s (N=1 per delay). Upstream with live connections: fast failure at +15 s, hang at +75 s. Never-bound 127.0.0.1 and localhost hung past 3 s; 127.0.0.2 and ::1 refused in under 4 ms.
  - Correction: Hanging is the default for a down loopback port on this host. The refused window depends on socket state and can last up to about 60 s. S2's main point stands, and its 50-400 ms figure should not be quoted.
- **contradicted** [S4] Orval has no types-only mode, so Kubb pluginTs is the types-only exit.
